shows.syn: David Beeves is a young Midwestern automobile mechanic, who discovers he is blessed with what appears to be almost supernatural good fortune that allows him to overcome every seemingly insurmountable obstacle that crosses his path, while those around him fall in defeat. David Beeves works as a self-taught auto mechanic in a barn that doubles as a repair station, where the entire first act takes place.

Narration by J. Morgan, Henry Ford, Booker T. Washington, Emma Goldman, Harry Houdini, and Evelyn Nesbit connect three families: an upper-class White family from New Rochelle – the Little Boy (Edgar), his Father (who runs a fireworks factory), Mother, Mother's Younger Brother, and Grandfather; a Black couple from Harlem in New York City – Sarah, who adores the pianist Coalhouse Walker Jr.

Glamorous but pretentious Oyster Bay, Long Island socialite Tracy Samantha Lord is planning a lavish June 1938 wedding to an equally pretentious executive, George Kittredge. Guests include her mother, grumpy little sister Dinah, and absent-minded Uncle Willy, who lives in a house near the Lord estate.

The play is set in a diner about 25 miles west of Kansas City in early March 1955. A freak snowstorm has halted the bus, and the eight characters (five on the bus) have a weather-enforced layover in the diner from approximately 1 am to 5 am. Romantic or quasi-romantic relationships include Grace and Carl, Professor Lyman and Elma, and Cherie and Bo.

A Delicate Balance is a three-act play by Edward Albee, written in 1965 and 1966. Premiered in 1966, it won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in 1967, the first of three he received for his work. They soon are followed by Agnes and Tobias's bitter 36-year-old daughter Julia, who returns home following the collapse of her fourth marriage.

"Beauty and the Beast" is a fairy tale written by the French novelist Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve and published anonymously in 1740 in La Jeune Américaine et les contes marins (The Young American and Marine Tales).
Villeneuve's original story was abridged, revised, and published by French novelist Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont in 1756 in Magasin des enfants (Children's Collection) which became the most commonly retold version.

Luis Alberto Molina, a gay window dresser, is in a prison in Argentina, serving his third year of an eight year sentence for corrupting a minor. He lives in a fantasy world to flee the prison life, the torture, fear and humiliation. His fantasies turn mostly around movies, particularly around a vampy diva, Aurora.

A pantomime of never-ceasing activities depicts the hustle and bustle of New York City ("Runyonland"). Three small-time gamblers, Nicely-Nicely Johnson, Benny Southstreet, and Rusty Charlie, argue over which horse will win a big race ("Fugue for Tinhorns"). The band members of the Save-a-Soul Mission, led by the pious and beautiful Sergeant Sarah Brown, call for sinners to "Follow the Fold" and repent ("Follow the Fold").

ct.n: George Bassman, Ted Royal and Michael Starobin

shows.syn: The musical opens with the recently deceased Morton in a state of limbo, looking back on his life. He is reluctantly guided by the mysterious 'Chimney Man,' who forces him to recall the more painful moments of his life when he attempts to ignore or embellish them. When his Creole grandmother discovers his new lifestyle, she disowns him.

shows.syn: In 1979 in New York City, Marvin, his ten-year-old son Jason, his psychiatrist Mendel, and his lover Whizzer are in the midst of an argument ("Four Jews in a Room Bitching"). Marvin explains the situation: he has left his wife Trina for a man, Whizzer, but no one is happy with his attempts to integrate Whizzer into the family ("A Tight-Knit Family").

La Bête is a 1991 comedy play by American playwright David Hirson. Written in rhymed couplets of iambic pentameter, the Molière-inspired story, set in 17th-century France, pits dignified, stuffy Elomire, the head of the royal court-sponsored theatre troupe, against the foppish, frivolous street entertainer Valere, whom the troupe's patron, Prince Conti, wishes them to bring aboard.

In Brooklyn in 1942, Evelyn Kurnitz has just died following a lengthy illness. She refuses. After a threat by Bella, she lets them stay without ever saying they could stay. Despite their grandmother owning and operating a candy store, Jay and Arty do not like their new living situation. Into their collective lives returns one of Eddie and Bella's other siblings, Louie Kurnitz, a henchman for some gangsters.

Carrie (also known as Carrie: The Musical) is a musical with a book by Lawrence D. Cohen, lyrics by Dean Pitchford, and music by Michael Gore. It is based on Stephen King's novel, and integrates elements from the 1976 film. The musical focuses on Carrie White, an awkward teenage girl with telekinetic powers, whose lonely life is dominated by her oppressive religious fanatic mother, Margaret.

ct.n: Anders Eljas, Harold Wheeler and Michael Starobin

shows.syn: Act One opens as the members of the Music Hall Royale circulate among the audience, introducing themselves to the patrons. More and more members of the company add to the growing noise until the music begins, and the Chairman of the proceedings bursts forth with the show's opening number, "There You Are".

Act I On 26 July 1952, a crowd in a Buenos Aires, Argentina theatre is watching a movie ("A Cinema in Buenos Aires, 26 July 1952") that is interrupted when news breaks of the death of First Lady Eva Perón. Both the crowd and the nation go into a period of public mourning ("Requiem for Evita") as Che, a member of the public, marvels at the spectacle and promises to show how Eva did "nothing for years" ("Oh What a Circus").

shows.syn: In the middle of the 19th century, Phineas Taylor (P. ) Barnum introduces his circus acts as he stands in front of a tent, proclaiming ("There Is a Sucker Born Ev'ry Minute"). He loves spectacle and excitement, using hype and "humbug" to promote his exhibits. His wife Charity disagrees with his use of "humbug" but loves him and aims to keep him grounded.

ct.n: Hamilton Deane and John L. Balderston

shows.syn: Act I, Scene 1 Sidney Bruhl, a previously successful playwright, has had a series of box office flops and is having trouble writing. Sidney mimics reading a play that he tells his wife, Myra, he has received from a student of his, Clifford Anderson. Sidney asserts that the student's play is a certain hit.

Velma Kelly is a vaudevillian who welcomes the audience to tonight's show ("All That Jazz"). Interplayed with the opening number, the scene cuts to February 14, 1928, in the bedroom of chorus girl Roxie Hart, where Roxie murders Fred Casely as he attempts to break off an affair with her.

ct.n: Bill Byers, Hershy Kay and Jonathan Tunick

shows.syn: In August 1946, Joe Keller, a self-made businessman, and his wife Kate are visited by a neighbor, Frank. At Kate's request, Frank is trying to figure out the horoscope of the Kellers' missing son Larry, who disappeared in 1943 while serving in the military during World War II. Joe and Kate react to this news with shock.

The show opens with two "actors," played by the same actors as the main characters of the play but considered different in the libretto, discussing which play they should perform. One actor suggests "the one about the man who kills his father and sleeps with his mother", but the other actor is in too good a mood for tragedy and they decide to perform a comedy instead.
After the Fall is a play by the American dramatist Arthur Miller.

Using the play within a play structure, Brooklyn focuses on a group of five ragtag homeless musicians known as the City Weeds. The group periodically transforms a street corner under the foot of the Brooklyn Bridge into a stage where they present their play about a Parisian singer, Brooklyn, named after the New York City borough from which her wayward father Taylor hailed.

The play takes place over the course of a single evening in the living room/kitchen of an isolated house shared by Jessie and her elderly mother Thelma. This evening, Jessie has carefully organized the house and made other detailed preparations for the future while explaining the changes to Thelma, who does not immediately notice anything unusual.

The play is set in 1904 at 1839 Wylie Avenue in Pittsburgh's Hill District. Aunt Ester, the drama's 285-year-old fiery matriarch, welcomes into her home Solly Two Kings, who was born into slavery and scouted for the Union Army, and Citizen Barlow, a young man from Alabama searching for a new life and in search of redemption.

Brian Wilson and The Beach Boys

shows.syn: In 1910s rural England, two young children, Jemima and Jeremy, are enthralled by the wreck of a champion racecar. When they learn it is due to be scrapped, they vow to ask their father, widower and eccentric inventor Caractacus Potts, to save it. They shortly meet the wealthy Truly Scrumptious, who drives them home to report their truancy to Caractacus; she leaves angered when he rejects her concerns.

Richard M. Sherman and Robert B. Sherman

shows.syn: The young woman Charity Hope Valentine is a taxi dancer at a dance hall called the Fandango Ballroom in New York City. With a shoulder bag and a heart tattooed on her left shoulder, Charity meets her boyfriend Charlie in Central Park. While Charlie silently preens himself, Charity speaks the pick-up lines she imagines him saying, and tells him how handsome he is ("You Should See Yourself").

shows.syn: A trio of 1960s street urchins named Crystal, Ronnette and Chiffon set the scene ("Little Shop of Horrors") and comment on the action throughout the show. Seymour Krelborn is a poor young man, an orphan living in an urban skid row. Audrey is a pretty blonde with a fashion sense that leans towards tackiness.

shows.t: Six Dance Lessons in Six Weeks
shows.syn: Lily Harrison is a self-described "tight-arsed old biddy" As the lessons continue, an improbable friendship develops out of their shared testiness and solitude.

shows.t: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof

shows.syn: The play takes place in New York in 1919. A young publisher named John Pace Seavering has enough money to publish one book. He is torn between two options - publishing the gargantuan novel of his former college roommate, Denis McCleary, who hopes that he and his fiancée, Rosamund Plinth, can win the blessing of her wealthy father - or publishing the memoirs of his lover Jessie Brewster, a famous singer.

shows.t: Oldest Living Confederate Widow Tells All

shows.syn: I Am My Own Wife is a play by Doug Wright based on his conversations with the German antiquarian Charlotte von Mahlsdorf. The one-person play premiered Off-Broadway in 2003 at Playwrights Horizons. It opened on Broadway later that year. The play was developed with Moisés Kaufman and his Tectonic Theater Project, and Kaufman also acted as director.

Tevye is a poor Jewish milkman in Czarist Russia. He and his bossy, sharp-tongued wife Golde have five daughters (eldest to youngest): Tzeitel, Hodel, Chava, Shprintze and Bielke. Tevye explains the customs of the Jews in the Russian shtetl of Anatevka in 1905, where their lives are as precarious as the perch of a fiddler on a roof ("Tradition").

shows.syn: The story centers around Akaash, a young man from the slums of Bombay who dreams of becoming the next big star in Bollywood. Fate steps in when a rich lawyer and his fiancée, an aspiring documentary filmmaker, arrive to prevent the demolition of Akaash's slum. Akaash quickly falls in love with the lawyer's fiancée, Priya, who happens to be the daughter of a famous Bollywood director.

shows.syn: Caroline, or Change is a musical with music by Jeanine Tesori and lyrics and book by Tony Kushner. The score combines spirituals, blues, Motown, classical music, and Jewish klezmer and folk music.

shows.syn: A Greek chorus introduces Princess Elsa of Arendelle, and her playful younger sister, Princess Anna ("Vuelie", "Let the Sun Shine On"). While the family knows about Elsa's magic, it is kept a secret from the people of Arendelle. One night at bedtime, Elsa and Anna build a magical snowman and name it Olaf ("A Little Bit of You"); Elsa creates snow in their room.

In the mid-1990s, the once-successful steel mills of Sheffield, South Yorkshire have shut down and most of the workers have been made redundant. Former steelworkers Gary "Gaz" Schofield and Dave Horsfall resort to stealing scrap metal from the abandoned mills and selling it to make money, taking Gaz's son Nathan with them for assistance, but a security guard keeps surprising them and locking them inside the mill.
Design for Living is a comedy play written by Noël Coward in 1932. It concerns a trio of artistic characters, Gilda, Otto and Leo, and their complicated three-way relationship.

A military tribunal convened in Nuremberg, Germany, involves four German judges and prosecutors standing accused of crimes against humanity for their involvement in atrocities committed under the Nazi regime. Dan Haywood heads a panel of Allied jurists who will hear and decide the case against the defendants.

The drama is set in a rural town in County Kerry, Ireland, that is overrun by a Hollywood film crew. The play centres around two friends, Charlie Conlon and Jake Quinn, employed as extras on the film. Charlie has aspirations to get his script made into a movie. Jake has recently returned from New York and is mesmerised, along with everyone else, by the star of the movie, Caroline.

Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve Apostles, worries that the followers of Jesus are getting out of control and may be seen as a threat by the Roman Empire, who might harshly suppress them ("Heaven on Their Minds"). The other apostles anticipate entering Jerusalem alongside Jesus and ask him about his plans, but Jesus tells them not to worry about the future.

The story follows Zorba as he talks his way into traveling with Nikos, a young American who has inherited an abandoned mine on Crete. Eventually, Zorba falls in love with a French woman, Hortense. Meanwhile, Nikos falls in love with The Widow. Tragedy ensues when Zorba loses all of his money to a belly dancer.

He announces to the audience, "White, a blank page or canvas. The challenge: bring order to the whole, through design, composition, tension, balance, light and harmony.

Anna Christie is the story of a former prostitute who falls in love, but runs into difficulty in turning her life around. The first act takes place in a bar owned by Johnny the Priest and tended by Larry. Coal-barge captain Old Chris receives a letter from his daughter, a young woman he has not seen since he lived in Sweden with his family and she was five years old.
*Let the Good Times Roll: A New Orleans Gumbo* is a new musical about the Big Easy and the vibrant souls there bringing the city to life.
The musical *Wanted* is the real-life story of Mary and Martha Clarke, sisters who strove to settle their mother’s sharecropper debt and save her home.

shows.t: Midnight In The Garden Of Good And Evil
shows.syn: Based on a bestselling book, *Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil* is a new musical about how a community in Savannah, Georgia responds to a local murder. Expect plenty of Southern charm — and even more Southern secrets.
*Galileo* is a new musical about an ancient story: a man, his discoveries, and the powers he challenged to fight for the truth.
*Dreamgirls* is a story of fame, and the musical journey, through love and loss, that guides three women toward it.

shows.syn: *10 Things I Hate About You* is a musical based on the film about teenage love in the suburbs.
*Dolly: An Original Musical* follows the life and career of a true music star, Dolly Parton. See, and hear, her story as you never have before in this new jukebox musical written by the icon herself.

shows.syn: *The Receptionist* is a wry and dark play about the complicity of evil, set in a modern office.

Heartfelt musical comedy about love, family, and drag, directed by Robert O’Hara. Set on the glittering French Riviera, this Tony Award–winning musical follows Georges and Albin, longtime partners who run a drag nightclub in St. Tropez. Their world is turned upside down when their son, Jean-Michel, announces his engagement to the daughter of conservative parents and invites them to dinner. This Encores! presentation revives the original 1983 orchestrations by Jerry Herman, heard live for the first time since the show’s Broadway debut. The creative team includes book writer Harvey Fierstein and composer-lyricist Jerry Herman, both Lifetime Achievement Tony Award recipients. Produced by New York City Center Encores!, the limited-run staging continues the company’s mission to celebrate and...
*Mexodus* is a groundbreaking hip-hop musical about people who escaped slavery by moving across the Mexican border.

Brian Quijada and Nygel D. Robinson

shows.syn: Relive all the funniest moments from the classic sitcom at this musical parody. See Jerry, George, Elaine, and Kramer's most iconic adventures set to hilarious songs like "The Master of their Domain," "Seasons of George," and "The Yadda Yadda Song."

A revenge tragedy centered on a Roman general whose victory ignites a cycle of brutality. The play follows Titus Andronicus, Rome’s most celebrated general, whose victory over the Goths sets off a relentless cycle of retaliation. After Titus sacrifices a member of the defeated enemy, Queen Tamora and her lover Aaron the Moor orchestrate a series of brutal reprisals that engulf Titus’s family and destabilize Rome itself. What begins as a triumph of state power descends into escalating violence, exposing how vengeance corrodes personal, political, and moral order. Written early in his career, Titus Andronicus is widely regarded as William Shakespeare’s bloodiest work. This production is directed by Jesse Berger and stars Patrick Page as Titus, one of Shakespeare’s most demanding tragic ro...

shows.syn: The Other Place is a play by American playwright Sharr White. The play premiered Off-Broadway in 2011 and then ran on Broadway.
*The Unknown* is a thrilling new play about a writer on the edge.

Returning home to assist her mother after a hospitalization, Haitian-American Bean soon finds her confidence shaken by her mother’s idea of what her life should be. Stuck at home, with nowhere to run from her mother’s ideas of marriage, motherhood, and malady, Bean must ask, “Do you know who you want to be? And are you brave enough to own it?” The Waterfall is an intimate and aching two-hander about the generational divides around family, womanhood, and the idea of the American Dream.
*Kenrex* is a true crime drama about Ken McElroy, a man from Missouri convicted of second-degree assault.

"Pied à Terre" is a captivating play that delves into the lives of two strangers who cross paths in a Parisian apartment. As they navigate the complexities of their temporary living arrangement, they find themselves grappling with their own personal demons and unexpected connections that challenge their preconceptions about love, loss, and the search for belonging in the City of Lights.

At a high school in Austin, Texas, four ninth-grade boys gather at lunchtime to make “spread,” or “Texas prison brick” from their snacks – dry ramen, hot chips, beef jerky, beans, hot water, all cooked in a bag.

Be there for this musical spoof on one of the most beloved sitcoms of all time. Go on an adventure with Chandler, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Monica, and Joey and hear all the iconic moments from TV set to hilarious parody songs.

When a nerdy flower shop worker finds a mysterious talking plant, it completely changes his life — but at a bloody cost. Go down to Skid Row for the latest revival of Alan Menken and Howard Ashman's horror comedy blossoming off Broadway.

"The Infinite Wrench" is a thrilling theatrical experience that challenges the boundaries of traditional storytelling. Performed by a skilled ensemble, the play presents a series of rapid-fire, wildly diverse sketches that explore the complexities of the human experience. From whimsical to poignant, each vignette offers a unique window into the unpredictable tapestry of life, leaving the audience exhilarated and deeply entertained.

shows.syn: *The Reservoir* is a new comedy about getting sober, getting your life together, and getting back into the rhythms of living in your hometown.
*Night Side Songs* is a communal musical experience in which actors play out the stories of healthcare workers and patients.
*Heathers* is a musical comedy based on the cult film and follows Veronica as she tries to navigate teenage issues, first love, and three Heathers who rule the school with an iron fist.

Accompanied onstage by musicians Erin Hill (harp/vocals) and Luke McCrosson (bass), Almond brings his journey to life with original songs that evoke his anxieties, hopes, and comic missteps, telling a humorous and profound story about fear and love.
*Mother Russia* is a sharp, dark comedy about a St. Petersburg spy who falls in love with the woman he is meant to track: an edgy artist with a mysterious past.

Ulysses is a 1705 tragedy by the British writer Nicholas Rowe. Rowe turned back to writing tragedies following his unsuccessful comedy The Biter of the previous year. The cast included Thomas Betterton as Ulysses, Barton Booth as Telemachus, Elizabeth Barry as Penelope and Anne Bracegirdle as Semanthe.

A world-premiere political drama directed by Doug Hughes. Set across decades of personal and political transformation, Public Charge follows Julissa, who immigrates from the Dominican Republic to the United States at age seven. After rising from a Wall Street law practice to serve as a senior official in the U.S. Department of State under Secretary Hillary Clinton, she confronts the human and moral complexities of public service—deploying aid to earthquake-stricken Haiti, navigating immigration politics, and negotiating the release of a wrongfully imprisoned American in Cuba. The play is co-written by former U.S. Ambassador Julissa Reynoso and award-winning playwright Michael J. Chepiga (The Rape of the Sabine Women, by Grace B. Matthias). Drawing from Reynoso’s firsthand experience in ...

Join Queenie's wild, gin-soaked 1920s party where desire and danger collide in a jazz-age tragedy. Set in the hedonistic world of late 1920s New York, The Wild Party follows Queenie, a vaudeville performer, and her volatile lover Burrs as they host a raucous party that spirals into chaos. Amid the haze of jazz, gin, and jealousy, the night exposes a crowd of guests chasing escape and excitement, only to confront bitter truths by morning. The musical is based on Joseph Moncure March’s once-banned narrative poem, whose raw depiction of excess and disillusionment shocked readers of its time. The production reunites composer and lyricist Michael John LaChiusa (The Gardens of Anuncia, Hello Again) and director George C. Wolfe (Jelly’s Last Jam) in a revival directed by Lili-Anne Brown, a two...

"Dirty Books" is a tantalizing exploration of forbidden desires and the power of the written word. Set in a covert library, the play follows a group of bibliophiles who uncover a cache of scandalous tomes, igniting a provocative journey into the depths of human passion and the consequences of their literary indulgences. As tensions rise and secrets unravel, the characters must confront the boundaries between pleasure and morality, challenging audiences to question the nature of their own darkest impulses.

The Adding Machine is a 1923 play by Elmer Rice.
The 2007 Columbia Encyclopedia of Modern Drama called it "a landmark of American Expressionism, reflecting the growing interest in this highly subjective and nonrealistic form of modern drama.

OnlyFans star attempts 1,000-subscriber stunt, exploring sex complexities via documentary maker. The play centers on Pollie, an OnlyFans creator who seeks significant fame by attempting an extreme public stunt: engaging sexually with 1,000 of her subscribers during the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. This premise reflects a current cultural climate where sex work is framed as highly competitive, leading to attention-seeking, extreme actions by creators vying for dominance in an oversaturated online market. The narrative acknowledges the recent viral nature of claims regarding high "body counts" and the resulting international debate among liberal feminists. The story is filtered through the perspective of an empathetic Documentary Maker, drawing focus to Pollie's complex relationship with se...
*Blood/Love* is a new pop opera about a vampire who falls in love with a mortal.

"Silver Manhattan" transports audiences to the glittering, high-stakes world of 1920s New York City. Amidst the Jazz Age opulence, a young stockbroker's meteoric rise is threatened by the alluring temptations of the underground and a web of deceit that could cost him everything. With dazzling visuals and a captivating narrative, this electrifying play takes theatergoers on a thrilling journey through the pulsing heart of the Big Apple.
John Thomas Harding is an American country music songwriter. He has written songs for Uncle Kracker, Kenny Chesney, Keith Urban, Blake Shelton, Dierks Bentley, and Darius Rucker.

A comic, insightful look at Deaf identity, co-written by James Caverly and Andrew Morrill. Tim and Jake are Deaf roommates living in a city apartment—but that’s about all they have in common. While one embraces Deaf culture with pride and resistance, the other seeks to navigate the hearing world with different priorities. As they clash over everyday tasks—like taking out the trash—their disagreement grows into a sharply comic, layered exploration of identity, communication, and what it really means to understand someone else’s experience. The play is co-written by James Caverly (known for Only Murders in the Building) and Andrew Morrill, both of whom bring personal insight and authenticity to the characters and their world. Directed by Nathaniel P. Claridad (Once Upon a Mattress at Tran...

shows.t: Antigone (This Play I Read in High School)
shows.syn: In this powerful adaptation of the ancient Greek tragedy, Antigone bravely defies the king's edict and honors her brother's memory, setting off a chain of events that threatens to tear her family and the city of Thebes apart. Torn between her loyalty to her brother and her duty to the state, Antigone must make an impossible choice that will test the boundaries of justice, morality, and the human spirit. This timeless tale of rebellion and the consequences of our actions comes to life on the stage, captivating audiences with its universal themes and poignant exploration of the human condition.

shows.syn: *Chinese Republicans* is a biting new satirical drama about the corporate ladder, a group of in-charge businesswomen, and the young woman who disrupts their perceptions of power and money.

Two actors and a Foley artist perform a live, shot-for-shot parody of the greatest dinosaur film of all time. A wildly inventive tour-de-force of comedy, physical theatre and live Foley.

shows.syn: Money, sex, and madness collide when exes reunite for a dinner party. The Amazing Sex Life of Rabbits follows two couples whose seemingly “friendly” dinner spirals into a volatile clash of love, lust, and class warfare. Bobby and Elise are struggling to keep their marriage—and their bank accounts—afloat when Bobby’s ex-wife, now a best-selling sex therapist, invites them to dinner with her new billionaire husband. What begins as an awkward reunion quickly devolves into a night of shocking revelations and psychological warfare, as the couples use every weapon at their disposal—nostalgia, sexuality, and money—to expose each other’s deepest desires and fears. This darkly comic new play unfolds as a modern-day morality test, examining what happens when ambition and desperation collide over ...
*Blackout Songs* is a new play about a couple who meets in AA and the journey of ups and downs they endure together.

When a billionaire becomes obsessed with immortality, ethical lines blur, power dynamics implode, and a shocking secret comes to light — one that turns the quest for longer life into a chilling examination of identity, consent, and what it really means to be human.

"La Llamada" () is a song recorded by American recording artist Selena for her first live album Live! It was composed by Selena y Los Dinos backup singer Pete Astudillo and Selena's brother and principal record producer A. Quintanilla III and produced by Quintanilla III and Argentine music producer Bebu Silvetti.

Pen Pals is a captivating theatrical journey that follows the unexpected bond between two strangers who begin corresponding through a chance encounter. As their connection deepens, the play explores the power of human connection and the transformative impact that can arise from the most unlikely of circumstances. Audiences are swept up in a heartwarming exploration of friendship, self-discovery, and the enduring resilience of the human spirit.
*Marcel on the Train* is a play about a young Marcel Marceau, one of the world’s greatest mimes, as he grows up in the shadow of rising Nazism during World War II.
*No Singing in the Navy* is a three-person, one-piano musical that spoofs and questions the Golden Age of Musicals.

Four estranged sisters reunite for a chaotic family ritual where secrets, humor, and grief collide. Jesa is a bold and emotionally charged new play that reimagines the idea of a “perfect family gathering.” When four estranged Korean American sisters return to Orange County to perform their father’s Jesa—a traditional ceremony honoring their ancestors—old resentments resurface, buried secrets are unearthed, and both literal and emotional ghosts demand to be faced. Blending sharp wit, explosive humor, and heartfelt honesty, the play explores the messy bonds of family, the weight of tradition, and the struggle to find connection amid conflict.

shows.t: The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee
shows.syn: *The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee* is a charming and witty musical about adolescent students competing to win a local spelling competition while coping with teenage issues along the way.
From the creators of the hit comedy DRUNK SHAKESPEARE comes The Greatest (Drunk) Love Story Ever Told: DRUNK ROMEO & JULIET!

Spend a day at Dunder Mifflin at this musical spoof on the hit sitcom. All the most famous lines and moments from the show appear in the stage musical, which features songs like “Goodbye Toby, You're the Worsty” and "That's What She Said."

One Sunday night, at the home of the wealthy Brents, psychiatrists living in a swanky Connecticut community, a woman shoots a man. By the time handsome detective James Ascher arrives, the body is gone. Ascher suspects the wife, Margaret Thorne Brent, a smart and sharp-tongued psychiatrist and novelist, although her patients are also suspect.

The hero of the drama, Arbenin, is a wealthy middle-aged man endowed with a rebellious spirit and a strong will. Born into high society, he strives in vain to gain independence and freedom. He lives by the laws of his society, and, in trying to defend his honor while blinded by jealousy and pride, ends up murdering his wife.

A haunting opera exploring trauma, loss, and buried secrets in the aftermath of a school shooting. Innocence, the final opera by Finnish composer Kaija Saariaho, is a powerful exploration of the lasting trauma caused by a school shooting. With a libretto by renowned author Sofi Oksanen, the opera unfolds through a hauntingly beautiful soundscape that blends traditional opera, expressionistic speak-singing, and Scandinavian folk music. Set a decade after the tragedy, the story follows a young couple whose wedding unexpectedly reopens old wounds, revealing long-buried secrets. At its core is a grieving mother, portrayed by mezzo-soprano Joyce DiDonato, and her lost daughter, sung by Finnish ethno-pop artist Vilma Jää. Conducted by Susanna Mälkki in Simon Stone’s strikingly direct producti...

A stage adaptation of Susanna Kaysen’s memoir set inside a 1960s psychiatric hospital. This world-premiere adaptation of Girl, Interrupted, written by Pulitzer Prize–winning playwright Martyna Majok, brings Susanna Kaysen’s memoir to the stage with original music by Aimee Mann and choreography by Sonya Tayeh. The play follows Susanna’s admission to a psychiatric institution, where she navigates an environment that functions as both a safe haven and a source of confinement. As she forms relationships with other young women in the ward, the work examines their efforts to regain structure, autonomy, and a sense of direction within the hospital’s constraints. Directed by Jo Bonney, the production presents a new dramatization of Kaysen’s account.
*Cold War Choir Practice* is an intriguing play about espionage, roller disco, and cults over a family reunion during the holidays.
*11 to Midnight* is a dance-theatre show about ringing in the new year with friends old and new, with promises to keep before time runs out.

shows.t: What We Did Before Our Moth Days
shows.syn: *What We Did Before Our Moth Days* is Wallace Shawn's new play about family and the kaleidoscopic journeys we make through remorse, sorrow, and joy.

Prince Hamlet of Denmark is the son of the recently deceased King Hamlet, and nephew of King Claudius, his father's brother and successor. Claudius hastily married King Hamlet's widow, Gertrude, Hamlet's mother, and took the throne for himself.

A daring Chekhov-inspired satire directed by Alexander Molochnikov, written by Eli Rarey. SEAGULL: TRUE STORY blends autobiographical drama and sharp political satire with the timeless human questions at the heart of Chekhov’s The Seagull. Written by Eli Rarey and created and directed by Alexander Molochnikov, this inventive retelling dramatizes Molochnikov’s own struggle to stage Chekhov’s masterpiece in the face of artistic and political constraints. What begins as a production of a classic play spirals into a collision of comedy, chaos, and creative defiance. Molochnikov—an internationally acclaimed director from the Moscow Art Theatre—leads an ensemble of international artists in this daring exploration of censorship, identity, and the relentless fight for artistic freedom. SEAGULL:...

Cold-case investigation unfolds through a hybrid of dance, theatre, and fractured memory. Set within an unresolved crime reopened after twelve years, Scorched Earth follows a detective re-examining an old case rooted in questions of land, legacy, and personal conflict. As the investigation revisits conflicting accounts, the detective and the primary suspect move through shifting layers of recollection, imagination, and unresolved tension. Inspired by John B. Keane’s The Field, the production blends elements of crime drama and psychological inquiry with movement-based storytelling. The creative team includes director, choreographer, and performer Luke Murphy, with design by Alyson Cummins, lighting by Stephen Dodd, and music by Rob Moloney, reuniting collaborators from the multi-award-wi...

Zachariah Munning has a natural sweetness that is unappreciated by his family. They long ago decided he was just lazy and dim. Zack’s calculating mother and cold-blooded brother are scheming to take advantage of a rich relative who is coming to visit. They believe her wealth might solve the problem of their failing business and are ready to sacrifice Zack for their own aims.

Charlie Price grows up as the fourth-generation scion in the family business, Price & Son, a shoe manufacturing company with its factory in Northampton. Another young boy, growing up in London, is as fascinated by shoes as Charlie is bored by them. But in this case, it is a pair of red women's heels that have attracted his attention, aggravating his strict father.

Benjamin Millepied’s dance-drama uses live cameras and rotating casts in a site-wide staging. This production utilizes handheld cameras to expand the scope of the performance beyond the limits of a conventional stage. Live video footage is transmitted to screens onstage, tracking the action as it unfolds in various tableaux and locations both backstage and throughout the Armory venue. The dance-drama explores the intersection between theatrical artifice and reality. It features a concise adaptation of Shakespeare’s narrative, focusing solely on the core elements: the undying devotion of the central couple and the intense emotional fallout. A distinct element of the production is the use of a rotating cast for the star-crossed lovers in each performance. This approach deliberately deviat...

Five Texas teens raise calves and navigate faith, girlhood, and competition in a rural barn. In a rural East Texas barn, five teenage girls prepare calves for competition while navigating the tangled terrain of adolescence. As they wrestle with school expectations, religious beliefs, and the complex rules of small-town life, their bonds are tested in unexpected ways. Faith, friendship, and survival collide in a world where tenderness can be as unruly as the animals they raise. Written by Libby Carr, Calf Scramble presents a darkly comedic take on the pressures of growing up under the gaze of both peers and tradition. The piece captures the distinctive rhythms of rural life, framing the girls’ struggles against a backdrop of competition and scripture. Produced by Primary Stages, the work...

shows.t: How My Grandparents Fell in Love, A Musical
shows.syn: A musical set in 1930s Rovno where a returning immigrant pursues a scholar amid rising antisemitism. Set in 1933, this musical follows Charlie, a Polish-born Jew who returns to Rovno after a decade in America to find a bride, and Chava, a young woman working in a hat shop who hopes to continue her studies. As Charlie attempts to court her, Chava remains focused on her academic ambitions while political tensions and antisemitism grow across Europe. The work is created by the team behind The Sabbath Girl: A New Musical and is based on a true story.

shows.v: The Marjorie S. Deane Little Theater
shows.syn: A musical revue of new songs about ageing, change, and life from Maltby and Shire. This musical revue navigates themes of ageing, memory, love, family, and the everyday quirks of life’s later chapters through an evening of interconnected songs. Drawing on decades of collaboration, the work presents vignettes about long-ago romance, ambitions past and present, relationships with grandchildren, lost keys, and the ongoing rhythm of human experience. Presented Off-Broadway at the Marjorie S. Deane Little Theater from late February through early April 2026, the revue completes a loose trilogy of song collections by Maltby and Shire that began with their earlier anthologies Starting Here, Starting Now and Closer Than Ever.

"The Porch on Windy Hill" invites audiences to a remote Appalachian homestead, where a family grapples with the weight of their past and the uncertain future. As they gather on the porch to confront long-buried secrets, the play explores themes of identity, belonging, and the power of personal narratives to shape our lives. Filled with raw emotion and evocative storytelling, this captivating drama offers a poignant glimpse into the lives of those often overlooked, challenging us to reckon with the complexities of the human experience.

shows.t: La Breve y Maravillosa Vida de Oscar Wao
shows.syn: The first-ever stage adaptation in Spanish of this renowned masterpiece.

shows.v: New York City Center - Stage II
shows.syn: LIL is a fighter, but not as well-known as her older brother BIG. What happens when she shows up on his doorstep and challenges him to a match?
The Dinosaurs is a piercing and funny look at female friendships, and the innately human battle between holding on and letting go.

shows.v: New York City Center – Stage I
shows.syn: *BIGFOOT! The Musical * is a musical myth about the small-town corruptions and paranoia that swirl around a misunderstood youth...who happens to be eight feet tall.

shows.v: The Griffin Theater at The Shed
shows.syn: *An Ark* is a first-of-its-kind theatrical experience where audiences look through mixed reality glasses, allowing starry performers to share stories about life directly to them.

shows.v: NYU Skirball Center for the Performing Arts

shows.syn: *Data* is a new play and suspenseful thriller about the darkest ambitions of Silicon Valley.

shows.v: Huron Club at the SoHo Playhouse

shows.t: Hans Litten: The Jew Who Cross-Examined Hitler

shows.syn: TOUCH, a solo play, stars Anthony Rapp as Syd Blatter, a middle aged gay failed writer and burnt-out 5th grade teacher whose life is upended when a meeting with a former student forces him down a rabbit hole of anxiety, regret and desire. At turns intense, hilarious, and moving, this intimate play forces the audience to confront the moral ramifications of everything we touch.

A two-hander comedy about heartbreak blending live music, science, and storytelling. The show follows Karin McCracken as a woman navigating the fallout of heartbreak, tracing a series of relationships, bad dates, and attempted reinventions. Opposite her, Simon Leary performs all the men in her life, shifting roles to reflect the recurring patterns and emotional echoes that define her experience. The narrative moves between humor and vulnerability, punctuated by lo-fi covers of well-known breakup songs that underscore the emotional terrain. Created by New Zealand company EBKM, the production integrates elements of science and technology to examine how heartbreak affects both body and mind. Through performance and music, the piece constructs a portrait of grief that situates romantic loss...

To booze or not to booze, that is the question at this hidden gem of the New York theatre scene. Even tragedies become comedies when four sober actors and one drunk one attempt to perform a Shakespeare play. The audience can even drink along.
Performed by the playwright and his mother, *Rheology* is a an expansive rumination on death, physics, and mother-son love.
*Jerome* is a new play about an aging gay couple who meets a stranger in their Arizona ghost town.

shows.v: Atlantic Theater Company - Linda Gross Theater
shows.syn: *Indian Princesses* is a touching and wise new play about a summer camp for young girls of color and their white fathers.

shows.t: El Último Sueño de Frida y Diego
shows.syn: Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera reunite on Día de los Muertos in this vivid, magical-realist opera. Gabriela Lena Frank’s first opera brings Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera’s love story to life in a stunning magical-realist tale. On Día de los Muertos, Frida returns from the underworld to reunite briefly with Diego, reliving their fiery passion and pain before parting once more. With a libretto by Pulitzer Prize winner Nilo Cruz, this visually striking production, inspired by their artwork, features Isabel Leonard and Carlos Álvarez under the baton of Yannick Nézet-Séguin. The Met premiere of Frank’s opera has been praised for its rich, imaginative score and vibrant storytelling.
*The Saviors* is a new play about faith, boyhood, and the bonds that break and tie.
*You Got Older* is a disarming play about a wayward daughter, her ailing father, and the strange connections she finds after returning home.
*Animal Wisdom* is a a musical séance like no other, a singular piece from Heather Christian blending storytelling, requiem, and family mythology.
*Burnout Paradise* is a unique theatrical experience in which four performers race on treadmills to get tasks done.

shows.v: The Newman Mills Theatre at the Robert W. Wilson MCC Theatre Space
shows.syn: *Birthright* is a new play about six friends, faith, and what it means to belong.
*My Joy is Heavy* is a musical memoir following a young family yearning for connection in the aftermath of a miscarriage.

Haley McGee sits atop a tall stool surrounded by six flower stems, each representing a different story from an imagined life. Audience members call out which tales they want to hear, shaping a semi-improvised meditation on aging, regret, and the ordinary moments that define us as McGee guides a hypothetical "you" from age 25 toward death. Only a portion of the twelve possible stories are told each performance, meaning no two shows are alike.
*||: Girls :||: Chance :||: Music :||* is about a prestigious girls’ music program in Berkeley where four teens meet and grow together.

shows.v: Lincoln Center Theater - Mitzi E. Newhouse Theater
shows.syn: *The Whoopi Monologues* revives the characters from Whoopi Goldberg's landmark 1984 Broadway solo show, reimagined by director Whitney White for a cast of five: Kerry Washington, Kara Young, Dominique Fishback, Danielle Pinnock, and Kecia Lewis.
*The Emporium* is Thornton Wilder's final play, tracing a man who goes on a life-changing journey.
*Bocking* is a new sex farce about what happens when two sets of parents come together after a playground incident go wrong.
*Bughouse* is a singular new play about the life of Henry Darger, a recluse and artist of unparalleled potential.
*TRU* is a solo show about a catastrophic night in the life of legendary author Truman Capote.

shows.v: The Griffin Theater at The Shed
shows.syn: Based on the beloved story, *Imitation of Life* is about two single mothers trying to build better lives for their daughters.

shows.t: Giulia: The Poison Queen of Palermo
shows.syn: A true story of deadly secrets, justice, and a woman on the edge of becoming a legend. A single act of self-defense sets off a chain of events that turns Giulia Tofana into one of history’s most notorious serial killers. As she fights to free women from the monsters around them, she must confront a haunting question—can she seek justice without losing herself in the process? This world premiere musical unravels a gripping true story, woven with dangerous secrets and life-altering consequences, all set to a powerful, contemporary score.
*Jackals* is Adam Rapp's futuristic thriller about a mother, her son, and the difficult decisions that inhibit their quest for survival.

shows.t: Going Bacharach: The Songs of an Icon

shows.syn: The West End transfer of Anaïs Mitchell's Tony Award-winning musical, a retelling of the ancient Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice set in a post-apocalyptic world.
Cole Escola's wickedly funny reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a woman desperate to become a stand-up comedian while her husband deals with some pesky Civil War business.
HAMILTON is an award-winning West End musical production about the life of Alexander Hamilton, the American Founding Father.
Now stumbling through its fourth catastrophic year, The Play That Goes Wrong is guaranteed to leave you aching with laughter!
