Andy Sachs lands a job as assistant to Miranda Priestly, the impossibly demanding editor-in-chief of fashion magazine Runway, navigating the cutthroat world of high fashion while struggling to maintain her integrity and personal relationships. As Andy climbs the professional ladder and becomes increasingly consumed by her work, she must choose between her ambitions and the life she's leaving behind. This musical adaptation captures Andy's transformation from aspiring journalist to fashion insider, exploring the costs of success in a glamorous but ruthless industry.

In June 1992, the cast members are preparing for rehearsals for Jackson's upcoming Dangerous World Tour; the first show in Munich, Germany is in two days. Rob, their manager, tells them to get into their places and warm up. Jackson arrives and watches the process, which leads to the opening number ("Beat It").

In 1950s Japan, two girls, Satsuki and Mei, whose mother has been hospitalised with tuberculosis, relocate to a village in the countryside. Their new house, in which they live with their professor father, Tatsuo, is haunted with soot spirits, , and they encounter Totoro, a "forest spirit who looks like the result of an experimental breeding programme involving a chinchilla, a barn owl and a bean-bag sofa".
Inspired by a true story, Kinky Boots follows Charlie Price, a young man who inherits his father's struggling shoe factory and finds an unlikely business partner in cabaret performer Lola.
Based on Michael Bond's beloved stories, Paddington follows the marmalade-loving bear from Peru as he arrives in London and finds a home with the Brown family.

A group of people at a graveyard mourn the passing of Emily Deetz. Emily's daughter, Lydia, reflects on the death of her mother and her own inability to be noticed by her father, Charles ("Prologue: Invisible"). A millennia-old demon named Beetlejuice appears and mocks the idea of living life to the fullest, as it will all be worthless once death comes ("The Whole 'Being Dead' Thing").
The story of Sister Rosetta Tharpe, the godmother of rock and roll, and her musical partnership with Marie Knight.

Avenue Q follows Princeton, a bright-eyed college graduate who comes to New York City with big dreams and a tiny bank account, finding his way in a neighbourhood full of colourful characters and puppets.
The Book of Mormon comes from South Park creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone, and Avenue Q co-creator Robert Lopez.

ct.n: Trey Parker, Robert Lopez & Matt Stone
Trey Parker, Robert Lopez & Matt Stone

shows.syn: As the sun rises, Rafiki the mandrill calls the animals to Pride Rock. She greets King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi before presenting their cub to the gathered animals ("Circle of Life"). Elsewhere, Mufasa's brother, Scar, laments his lost chance at becoming King. Back at her baobab tree, Rafiki paints an image of the cub and asks the spirits to conjure the new prince's name: Simba.
A mother. A daughter. 3 possible dads. And a trip down the aisle you'll never forget!
Grab your skateboard, stock up on plutonium and turn the ignition on your DeLorean because Back to the Future is landing in the West End!
Based on Charles Dickens' Oliver Twist, this beloved musical follows orphan Oliver as he navigates the streets of Victorian London, from the workhouse to Fagin's gang of young pickpockets.
David Hare's play set at a Cambridge May Ball in 1969, following a rock band hired to perform as the evening descends into chaos.
A political comedy set in Downing Street, exploring the absurdities and machinations of modern British politics.
A new play exploring themes of faith, redemption and human connection.
Alan Ayckbourn's darkly comic play about Susan, a vicar's wife whose fantasy family starts to feel more real than her actual one.

In 1815 France, Jean Valjean, "Prisoner 24601", is released on parole by guard Javert after 19 years hard labor in prison for stealing bread ("Work Song (Look Down)"). Marked by his yellow ticket of leave ("On Parole"), Valjean is shunned and cannot find decent work until the Bishop of Digne offers him shelter.

In the Montmartre Quarter of Paris, France, at the turn of the 20th century, the Moulin Rouge cabaret club, "where all your dreams come true", is in full swing under the direction of Harold Zidler. Christian arrives with fellow bohemians Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec and Santiago the Argentinean. The money-motivated Duke of Monroth is introduced ("Welcome to the Moulin Rouge").

Roald Dahl's Matilda, also known simply as Matilda and Matilda the Musical, is a musical with music and lyrics by Tim Minchin and a book by Dennis Kelly. It is based on the 1988 novel Matilda by Roald Dahl.
Robert Icke directs a new West End production of Shakespeare’s tragedy starring Sadie Sink and Noah Jupe at the Harold Pinter Theatre.
The world’s longest running play re-opens in the West End with an all-star cast.

A brand-new musical comedy is created live in front of your very eyes at each performance of this multi award-winning show, as audience suggestions are instantly transformed into hilarious all-singing, all-dancing entertainment.

Set in a field in rural Essex in the summer of 1536, three young women — Anna, Jane and Mariella — meet at their childhood gathering place to trade gossip as word arrives from London of Anne Boleyn's arrest and execution. As the distant violence against a fallen queen seeps into their own lives, the three friends face choices that all carry the threat of violence. Ava Pickett's debut play, winner of the 2024 Susan Smith Blackburn Prize and directed by Lyndsey Turner, is a funny and devastating portrait of female friendship in a world stacked against women.

Paranormal Activity is a horror play written by Levi Holloway, based on the film series of the same name, set in the world of the film series. The play premiered at Leeds Playhouse in July 2024, and had its West End premiere at the Ambassadors Theatre on 5 December 2025.
William Nicholson's moving drama about C.S. Lewis and his unexpected late-in-life love affair with American poet Joy Davidman.
Arthur Miller's devastating drama about a family confronting the consequences of wartime profiteering, as the sins of the father threaten to destroy everything he has built.

shows.t: Austentatious: An Improvised Jane Austen Novel
shows.syn: The award-winning improv comedy troupe creates a brand new Jane Austen novel from scratch at every performance, based on a title suggested by the audience.
The story of Frank Sinatra, from his humble beginnings in Hoboken to becoming one of the most iconic entertainers of the 20th century, featuring his legendary songs.
Edmond Rostand's classic tale of the brilliant, big-nosed swordsman-poet who helps another man woo the woman he secretly loves.

shows.t: Harry Potter And The Cursed Child: Both Parts
shows.syn: Wands at the ready! Step into the Wizarding World of Harry Potter for the much-anticipated continuation of the beloved book series, set nineteen years later. Magic will come to life before your very eyes in this spellbinding two-part adventure with Harry, Ron, and Hermione.

Six (stylised SIX in all caps) is a musical with music, book, and lyrics by Toby Marlow and Lucy Moss. It is a modern retelling of the lives of the six wives of Henry VIII, presented in the form of a singing competition/pop concert.
We use cookies to personalise your experience, including improving the quality of your show recommendations. By clicking "accept all", you consent to our cookie policy.

In New York in 1959, theatre producer Max Bialystock opens Funny Boy, a musical version of Hamlet. Reviews are overwhelmingly negative, and the show closes after one performance ("Opening Night"). Max, who was once called the King of Broadway, tells a crowd of down-and-outs of his past achievements and vows to return to form ("King of Broadway").
Set in 1959 Hawkins, Indiana, this stage prequel to the hit series follows a young Jim Hopper, Bob Newby, Joyce Maldonado, and Henry Creel as darkness takes root in their town.
Mischief Theatre's hilarious comedy about the Cornley Drama Society's disastrous attempt to stage a 1920s murder mystery.

shows.t: The Spy Who Came In From The Cold
shows.syn: Based on John le Carré's seminal Cold War thriller, a British intelligence agent is sent on one final, dangerous mission behind the Iron Curtain.

shows.t: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
shows.syn: Based on Rachel Joyce's bestselling novel, Harold Fry sets out to post a letter and instead walks 600 miles across England to save an old friend.

shows.t: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind
shows.syn: Based on the true story of William Kamkwamba, a teenager in Malawi who saved his village from famine by building a windmill from scrap parts and library books.

shows.t: Black Is The Color Of My Voice
shows.syn: Apphia Campbell's one-woman show about Nina Simone, charting the singer's journey from child prodigy to civil rights icon through her extraordinary music.

Don’t miss *High Noon*, a thriller like none other, as it brings one of the most iconic westerns to life on stage. Starring Billy Crudup and Denise Gough, this gripping West End premiere counts down to what feels like an impossible choice.

Beneath the Paris Opera House lurks the Phantom, a disfigured musical genius who becomes obsessed with Christine Daaé, a young soprano he secretly tutors and propels to stardom. When Christine rekindles her romance with the dashing Vicomte Raoul de Chagny, the jealous Phantom unleashes terror upon the opera company, eventually abducting Christine to his subterranean lair. There, she must confront the man behind the mask and choose between pity for her tormentor and love for Raoul.

Starlight Express has been revised many times since it was first produced. These revisions range from tweaks to lyrics to adding or removing entire songs, characters and subplots. The fundamental story, however, has stayed the same. This synopsis reflects the show as it was first produced, in the West End in 1984.

The Narrator introduces the main characters in the story. Cinderella wishes to attend a festival held by the king, much to the dismay of her Stepmother and Stepsisters. Jack wishes his cow, Milky White, would give milk, and his Mother wishes that Jack would sell Milky White. A Baker and his Wife wish to have a child, and Little Red Riding Hood wishes for bread to bring to her ill Grandmother.

Witness for the Prosecution is a play adapted by Agatha Christie from her 1925 short story "Traitor's Hands". The play opened in London on 28 October 1953 at the Winter Garden Theatre (although the first performance had been in Nottingham on 28 September). It was produced by Sir Peter Saunders.

"Manic Street Creature" is a captivating musical that takes audiences on a wild journey through the bustling streets of a city. Blending heart-pounding dance numbers and powerful original songs, the show follows a diverse group of characters as they navigate the challenges and exhilaration of urban life, discovering the strength to confront their inner demons and forge unexpected connections. With its electric energy and poignant storytelling, "Manic Street Creature" promises to leave theatergoers enthralled and deeply moved.
The world premiere of Ben Ockrent's blackly comic drama explores the legacies we inherit, the choices we make and the true cost of family secrets, directed by Olivier Award winner Michael Longhurst.

Driftwood is the first play from Martina Laird. Directed by Chichester Festival Theatre’s Artistic Director Justin Audibert and set in 1950s Caribbean, it’s a deeply evocative story of self-determination and the search for family and belonging.

Pride is an upcoming musical with book and lyrics by Stephen Beresford and music by Christopher Nightingale, Josh Cohen and DJ Walde. The musical is based on Beresford's 2014 film of the same name which in turn is depicts the true story of the Lesbians and Gays Support the Miners campaign during the British miners' strike in 1984.

ct.n: Christopher Nightingale, Josh Cohen, DJ Walde

shows.syn: A 90th birthday party that no-one seems to want. Four generations of Northern Irish women, reunited under one roof.
A life affirming play about the elusive connection between loss and rebirth.
A bittersweet, tender exploration of the long tail of grief and the fickleness of memory, Heart Wall asks where we go when the walls start closing in and home has become somewhere you don’t know.
Don’t miss the world premiere of *Sweetmeats*, a touching tale of unlikely love between two South Asian elders by award-winning playwright Karim Khan.
Hilarious and heart-breaking - will have you laughing one minute and crying the next. Written by Piers Black and directed by Bryony Shanahan.

The Octagon Room in Sir Robert Chiltern's house in Grosvenor Square Sir Robert – a member of the House of Commons and junior government minister – and his wife, Lady Chiltern, are hosting a gathering that includes his friend Lord Goring, a dandified bachelor, Chiltern's sister Mabel and other guests.
This urgent new play by Sophie Swithinbank directed by Nancy Medina casts a scathing light on the systemic injustice that permeates the very institutions sworn to protect us.

Jaja’s African Hair Braiding in Harlem is a salon full of funny, whip-smart, talented women ready to make you look and feel nice-nice. Every day, a lively and eclectic group of West African immigrant hair braiders are creating masterpieces on the heads of neighborhood women. Just like her mother, Dreamer Marie is trying to secure her future; she’s just graduated high school and all she wants to do is go to college.

shows.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest
shows.syn: Inside a psychiatric facility, Chief Bromden has been silent for years — confined and maligned by a system that labels, divides and forgets. But he has a story to tell. He’s just been waiting for someone to listen.

Don’t miss *Deep Azure*, the late Academy Award and BAFTA-nominated actor and writer Chadwick Boseman’s powerhouse of a play, during its UK premiere at the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse, directed by the masterful Tristan Fynn-Aiduenu.

Best friends George and Harold have been creating comics for years, but now that they’re 10, they figure it's time to level up and write a musical based on their favourite character, Dog Man, the crime-biting sensation who is part dog, part man, and ALL HERO!! How hard could it be?

shows.t: Mother Courage and Her Children - Globe
shows.syn: Shakespeare’s Globe welcomes revolutionary playwright Brecht to the stage for the very first time with a new production of his anti-war masterpiece, Mother Courage and Her Children.
In this vibrant new production of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream, the Globe Theatre becomes a space for communal celebration under starry, summer skies.

When Brian Epstein steps into the Cavern Club, he finds more than just a band – he finds his life’s calling. Captivated by the charismatic frontman, John Lennon, Brian sets out to make the Fab Four the most famous group on earth.

shows.t: The Playboy of the Western World
shows.syn: On the west coast of County Mayo Christy Mahon stumbles into Flaherty's tavern. There he claims that he is on the run because he killed his own father by driving a loy into his head. Flaherty praises Christy for his boldness, and Flaherty's daughter (and the barmaid), Pegeen, falls in love with Christy, to the dismay of her suitor, Shawn Keogh.
Run wild and free in the muddy magic of the woods this summer with this euphoric new production of Shakespeare’s As You Like It in the Globe Theatre.

Les Liaisons Dangereuses () is an 1985 play by Christopher Hampton adapted from the 1782 novel by Pierre Choderlos de Laclos. The plot focuses on the Marquise de Merteuil and the Vicomte de Valmont, rivals who use sex as a weapon of humiliation and degradation, all the while enjoying their cruel games.
As the lines blur between entertainment and abuse, technology and sex, violence and voyeurism - who’s complicit and who is in control? And are you watching?

shows.t: Between The River and The Sea
shows.syn: Yousef was raised as a Christian-Arab-Palestinian-Israeli kid in Haifa, and is now raising two Jewish-Arab-Austrian kids in Berlin. Only he’s facing a custody battle, so things are getting complicated...
This Summer, see Shakespeare’s Love’s Labour’s Lost as you’ve never experienced it before, in this blazing, flamenco-inspired new production.

From Olivier and Tony Award-Winning playwright Richard Nelson (Farewell to the Theatre, Goodnight Children Everywhere), Springwood is a witty and poignant new play that pulls back the curtain on a pivotal meeting where the personal and political entwine.

Judy Garland is staying in London, along with young new fiancé Mickey Deans and loyal friend and pianist Anthony, preparing for her five-week run of shows at The Talk of the Town. Garland hopes that her act will help her maintain her star profile, especially considering a recent string of bad press against her.

shows.t: Dirty Dancing: The Classic Story on Stage
shows.syn: Get Ready for the ‘Time of Your Life’ as the record-breaking Dirty Dancing the Classic Story on Stage becomes the opening production at the Capital Theatre, Westfield London from 16 October 2026.
Don’t miss this brilliant restaging of William Shakespeare’s *The Tempest*, directed by and starring Tim Crouch. The stunning play turns one island into a gorgeous theatrical landscape.

The play is a study of a ruthless, sociopathic businessman: his inability to love and the impact of this on others (notably, his son and his wife). The central character Gregor Antonescu was based on the lives of Ivar Kreuger, the Swedish Match King, and Samuel Insull the Anglo-American investor.
Bullock Creek, South Carolina, 1862: Ginnie Good raises five children in a cabin as a war rages outside. Today: A woman rents the cabin on AirBnB to conjure her ancestors.
A group of teenage revolutionaries, including Gavrilo Princip, are swept up in a scheme to assassinate Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

The Rosenbergs of Edgware are a family in crisis. David is desperately trying to save a failing catering business; Lesley is trying to save a failing husband, and their daughter Ruth is facing public vilification for investigating war crimes in Gaza for the UN, is she failing her community? Will any of them succeed?

The Enormous Crocodile is weaving his way through the jungle in search of delicious little fingers and squidgy podgy knees… Only the other jungle creatures can foil his secret plans and clever tricks, but they’re going to have to find a large amount of courage to stop this greedy brute.

Copenhagen is a play by Michael Frayn, based on an event that occurred in Copenhagen in 1941, a meeting between the physicists Niels Bohr and Werner Heisenberg, who had been Bohr's student. It premiered in London in 1998, at the National Theatre, running for more than 300 performances, starring David Burke (Niels Bohr), Sara Kestelman (Margrethe Bohr), and Matthew Marsh (Werner Heisenberg).

Don’t miss Noël Coward’s first-ever but most rarely seen show, *The Rat Trap*, a dark and witty drama focused on marriage as it is reimagined for its centenary year, with revisions by Bill Rosenfield and directed by Kirsty Patrick Ward.

Summerfolk () is a play by Maxim Gorky written in 1904 and first published in 1905 by Znaniye (1904 Znaniye Anthology, book Three), in Saint Petersburg. Full of characters who "... might have stepped out of a Chekhovian world", it takes place in 1904—the same year that Anton Chekhov died. The play dramatises the Russian bourgeois social class and the changes occurring around them.

The play tells the story of Nikolai Ivanov, a man struggling to regain his former glory. For the past five years, he has been married to Anna Petrovna, a disinherited Jewess, who has become very ill. Ivanov's estate is run by a distant relative, Mikhail Borkin, who is frequently advising people on how he can help them make money.

With the eyes of the world watching, a Welsh farming community, torn apart by tragedy, gathers to debate a planned memorial. Tonight, you’re in the village hall with them – and every vote counts. A portrait of a close-knit community wrestling with its past, its future and the politics of remembrance.

Inspired by letters and diaries from Monet and his peers, A Mirrored Monet immerses audiences in the cafés, studios, and salons of Belle Époque Paris, with music and projections bringing the era vividly to life.

shows.t: It Walks Around The House At Night
shows.syn: In a quiet suburban home, a family is haunted by a mysterious presence that stalks the halls at night. As they grapple with the unsettling occurrences, the boundaries between the natural and supernatural worlds begin to blur, leaving them to confront their deepest fears and uncover the chilling truth behind the house's dark history.

Five young women running on pop music, optimism, and fury are about to shed light on the darkest secrets in their small town. A story about girlhood, power, and questioning the narratives we’ve been taught.
On his 69th birthday, a man sits alone and listens to the echoes of his younger self.

In 1809, Thomasina Coverly, the daughter of the house, is a precocious teenager with ideas about mathematics, nature, and physics well ahead of her time. She studies with her tutor Septimus Hodge, a friend of Lord Byron (an unseen guest in the house). As their studies unfold – with the help of Valentine Coverly, a post-graduate student in mathematical biology – the truth about what happened in Thomasina's time is gradually revealed.

In 1930s Germany, a woman puts on her dead husband’s trousers and never takes them off. As the world around her changes, she endures war and dictatorship, hunger and humiliation – always fighting to stay alive.

shows.t: Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club
shows.syn: Life is a cabaret, old chum! Don't miss this revival of a Kander and Ebb classic, and be immersed into the Kit Kat Club with the incredible transformation of the Playhouse Theatre. Leave all your troubles at the door and see this seven-time Olivier Award-winning production of *Cabaret* in London's West End.

Deep in the desolate wilderness stands a crumbling castle with a mysterious presence lurking within. TONY nominee Kip Williams' intoxicating reimagining of Bram Stoker's immortal gothic horror stars Cynthia Erivo, who transforms into all 23 roles in this blood-pumping solo adaptation.
The music was composed by Alan Menken, with lyrics by David Zippel.

In 1943, Naval intelligence officer Ewen Montagu welcomes the audience to MI5, where the "elite" of the British military contribute to the World War II effort ("Born to Lead"). Montagu reads his plan, and despite declaring it "insane", recognises its potential and convinces Charles that they should team up to pitch Mincemeat to Bevan, noting his own natural "flair for presentation" ("Dead in the Water (Reprise)").

ct.n: David Cumming, Felix Hagan, Natasha Hodgson & Zoë Roberts
David Cumming, Felix Hagan, Natasha Hodgson & Zoë Roberts

shows.syn: The award-winning musical, *Titanique*, which combines the Academy Award Winning film, *Titanic*, with the music of Céline Dion in a laugh-out-loud funny production, has its West End debut at the Criterion Theatre.

An unnamed British-American rock band gathers at a recording studio in Sausalito to record their second album, assisted by sound engineers Grover and Charlie. Drummer Simon, whose wife and children still live in England, attempts to keep the peace as the marriage between bassist Reg and keyboardist/vocalist Holly crumbles, largely due to Reg's drug and alcohol addiction.

Céline Dion crashes a Titanic museum tour, insisting she was actually aboard the doomed ocean liner and proceeding to retell the story her way. As she hijacks the narrative, she recasts the romance between Jack and Rose alongside characters like the Iceberg, Victor Garber, and Ruth, belting Dion's greatest hits while competing with Rose for control of the tale and Jack's affections.

ct.n: Marla Mindelle, Constantine Rousouli & Tye Blue
Marla Mindelle, Constantine Rousouli & Tye Blue

shows.syn: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society, fresh from hits such as Two Sisters, The Lion and The Wardrobe, Cat, and James and the Peach, has received a substantial bequest and is putting on a performance of The Murder at Haversham Manor – a 1920s murder mystery play, similar to The Mousetrap, which has the right number of parts for its members.
A riveting evening of mind-blowing, interactive magic, hosted by Steve Cohen. Take part in this unusual and perfect date night experience.

In 19th-century Paris, the celebrated courtesan Violetta Valéry abandons her glittering life of pleasure for the devoted love of young Alfredo Germont. Their happiness is shattered when Alfredo's father, Giorgio, secretly persuades Violetta to leave his son to protect the family's honor. Believing himself betrayed, Alfredo publicly humiliates her, only to learn the truth too late, reuniting with the dying Violetta as tuberculosis claims her life.

shows.t: Hugo Marchand | Artists at the Center

shows.syn: Following her acclaimed 2024 company debut in Puccini’s Madama Butterfly, soprano Asmik Grigorian returns to the Met as Tatiana, the lovestruck young heroine in this ardent operatic adaptation of Pushkin. Baritone Igor Golovatenko reprises his portrayal of the urbane Onegin, who realizes his affection for her all too late. The Met’s evocative production, directed by Tony Award–winner Deborah Warner, “offers a beautifully detailed reading of … Tchaikovsky’s lyrical romance” (The Telegraph).

Direct from London’s West End, Jamie Allan’s Amaze is New York City’s must-see magic sensation. Bold, heartfelt, and unlike anything you’ve experienced before, Amaze blends 80s nostalgia with jaw-dropping, high-tech illusions to create a show that doesn’t just amaze - it moves you.
*Magic Mike Live* is a ninety-minute saucy dance spectacular inspired by the *Magic Mike* films.

shows.t: I Wish My Life Were Like A Musical
shows.syn: A comedic musical revealing the hilarious highs and lows of life as a theatre performer. I Wish My Life Were Like A Musical is a cheeky, song-filled look behind the curtain of musical theatre, charting the journey from eager drama school hopeful to seasoned diva, chorus veteran, or forgotten performer. With sharp humor and affectionate honesty, the show exposes everything performers never admit—from disastrous auditions and grueling choreography to backstage rivalries, fan encounters, and the rare onstage moments that make it all worthwhile. After earning numerous awards, multiple international productions, and even a filmed version for streaming, this hit revue brings its trademark mix of charm, chaos, and industry insider wit to New York’s SoHo Playhouse in 2026.

Aboard a ship bound for Cornwall, the Irish princess Isolde is being delivered as a bride to King Marke by the knight Tristan, though she and Tristan harbor a forbidden love ignited by a shared potion. Their secret affair is betrayed at Marke's court, and Tristan is mortally wounded in the ensuing confrontation. Isolde arrives at his Breton castle only as he dies, and she joins him in transfigured death.

shows.v: LCT3 at the Claire Tow Theater
shows.syn: *A Woman Among Women* centers on Cleo, founder of the local women’s wellness group, as she tries to hold her fragile community together.
After taking the West End by storm and selling out night after night, Burlesque is back in town!

Successful lawyer, Atticus Finch, encourages kindness and empathy in his children, but is pushed to the limits of these qualities himself when he resolves to uncover the truth in a town that seems determined to hide it.

shows.t: Jim Henson’s Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock LIVE
Here There Are Blueberries (Theatre Royal Stratford East)
shows.syn: At the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, archivist Rebecca Erbelding receives a mysterious photo album from a former US Army officer, its pages revealing candid snapshots of SS officers relaxing at Auschwitz. As her team of historians works to identify the smiling perpetrators and the resort-like retreat where they unwound, the investigation forces a reckoning with the ordinary humanity of those who carried out atrocity.

After being pushed over the edge by the most popular kids at school, four-eyed wallflower Nancy Nelson cries to the heavens for help! But it is Satan who hears her cry. The Devil transforms Nancy into a big-haired, foul- mouthed, sex bomb rocker who's hungry for souls, and sweet revenge is on the menu! Who will save Nancy? And will the power of love for who she really is break the spell before its too late?

The play follows the England men's football team under Gareth Southgate in the run-up to, and aftermath of, three tournaments: its unexpected run to the semifinals at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, its disappointing defeat in the 2020 European Championship final at Wembley Stadium, and its quarterfinal exit from the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Three friends spring across a vibrant city, life is new, exciting and undiscovered. As summer speeds towards them they grasp the metropolis and push, push, push through to autumn. What will be discovered and what will life bring as they reach the depths of winter?

What prompts a 17-year-old boy to blind six horses? This is the challenge presented to psychiatrist Martin Dysart as he delves into the psyche of his young patient Alan Strang to search for the answers and at the same time questioning whether the cure is more dangerous than the crime.
An exploration of life, loss and a single question: Where does true inspiration come from?
This summer, the hotly anticipated world premiere of Death Note: The Musical, arrives at the Barbican for 50 performances only from 30 July to 12 September.

shows.t: Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes
shows.syn: College professor and acclaimed writer Jon is in a rut — he's in middle age and in the middle of another divorce — until Annie, a student and admirer, enters his life. What follows is a slippery battle for power and self-control.
A massage therapist's routine unravels when a mysterious client disrupts his ordered life.
An immersive theatrical adaptation of Suzanne Collins' bestselling novel, bringing the world of Panem to life in a custom-built arena at Canary Wharf.
Arthur Miller's powerful drama about the paralysis of fear in the face of injustice, set in Brooklyn 1938 as events in Nazi Germany begin to ripple across the Atlantic.
Rosamund Pike stars in a new play at Wyndham's Theatre, from the team behind Prima Facie.

A couple’s Ugandan getaway turns perilous in this darkly comic tale of love and survival. Silverback Mountain is a darkly humorous adventure exploring love, identity, and resilience amid cultural clash and political danger. Mickey, a high-strung New York artist, and his exuberant husband Andy travel to Uganda on a dream “bucket list” journey to see mountain gorillas, hoping for romance and escape. But their trip quickly takes a dangerous turn in a country where homosexuality is criminalized, forcing the couple to confront fear, prejudice, and unexpected challenges. As paradise becomes perilous, they must rely on courage, humor, and their bond with each other to survive an experience that tests both their relationship and their sense of freedom.
Two couples. A tangle of secrets. And a truth nobody is ready to face.
*The Maids* is a riveting drama about two maids who plan the murder of their master.

Nicole Travolta recounts debt, reinvention, and Hollywood oddities in a solo comedy. A solo performance tracing a period of personal and financial upheaval, the show follows a woman navigating debt, addiction, divorce, and the pressures attached to a famous last name. In an effort to stabilize her life, she takes an unexpected job spray tanning clients in Hollywood, where encounters with performers, influencers, and industry personalities provide the material for a series of character-driven stories and impressions. The piece blends stand-up comedy with autobiographical storytelling as the performer reconstructs the experiences that reshaped her sense of identity.

Bill Bailey returns with a show that celebrates this great tradition, as the versatile multi-instrumental, multi-lingual, purveyor of humour and musical prowess, who could lay claim to being perhaps the foremost practitioner of this great tradition… An entertainer, a performer, a modern Vaudevillean!
A psychological thriller by Winsome Pinnock. Harford Hall holds secrets. New inheritor Fenella calls in experts Marva and Abi to authenticate diaries which may reveal truths.
World premiere by Fran Kranz. Two couples meet in the side room of a church. Can they heal a violent divide.

The setting is the Islaev country estate in the 1840s. Natalya Petrovna, a headstrong 29-year-old, is married to Arkadi Islaev, a rich landowner seven years her senior. Bored with life, she welcomes the attentions of Mikhail Rakitin as her devoted but resentful admirer, without ever letting their friendship develop into a love affair.

In County Durham, the 1984–85 coal miners' strike is just beginning ("The Stars Look Down"). Motherless eleven-year-old Billy Elliot stays behind after his boxing class to give keys to Sandra Wilkinson, who runs a ballet class. The class is all girls, but Billy is attracted to the grace of the dance ("Shine").

gather every year to make the "Jellicle choice" and decide which cat will ascend to the Heaviside Layer and come back to a new life. After the overture, a tribe of cats known as the Jellicles gather on stage and describe themselves and their purpose ("Jellicle Songs for Jellicle Cats"). This is followed by a ballet solo performed by Victoria to signal the beginning of the Jellicle Ball ("The Invitation to the Jellicle Ball").

ct.n: T. S. Eliot, Trevor Nunn, Richard Stilgoe

shows.syn: DARK OF THE MOON is a supernatural tale of powerful witchcraft, small-town prejudices and the power of love.
Witty and heartbreakingly human, Evening All Afternoon is a story about things lost and things remembered and how sometimes, in order to live, you have to face what’s no longer there.

Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve Apostles, worries that the followers of Jesus are getting out of control and may be seen as a threat by the Roman Empire, who might harshly suppress them ("Heaven on Their Minds"). The other apostles anticipate entering Jerusalem alongside Jesus and ask him about his plans, but Jesus tells them not to worry about the future.

As the world’s great powers set their sights on the moon, a schoolteacher gathers a group of misfit dreamers and trains them for lift-off. The true(ish) story of the Zambian Space Program, and a nation’s defiant dream to reach for the stars.

A night-shift officer races to save a caller in a real-time emergency thriller. This real-time thriller centers on Joe, a troubled police officer working the night shift, who receives a 999 call from a woman named Emily. As the call unfolds, Joe attempts to piece together fragmented information to locate and assist her, navigating mounting tension and uncertainty. Confined largely to the control room, the drama builds through voice, inference, and rapidly shifting assumptions, as Joe begins to suspect that the situation may not be as straightforward as it first appears. The play stars Russell Tovey as Joe and is directed by Felix Barrett. Written by Chloë Moss, it is based on the films Den Skyldige and The Guilty.

shows.t: The Guy Who Didn't Like Musicals
shows.syn: A group of singing "zombies" addresses the audience, setting the scene in the small town of Hatchetfield and introducing the eponymous "Guy Who Didn't Like Musicals", unremarkable everyman Paul Matthews ("The Guy Who Didn't Like Musicals"). Paul works at an office with his coworkers Bill, Charlotte, and Ted.
Sandra Oh takes the title role in a razor-sharp reimagining of Molière’s classic.

Tracey Scott Wilson’s seminal newsroom thriller is directed by Clint Dyer (Death of England) with a cast including BAFTA Award-winner Letitia Wright (Black Panther), Ashley Thomas (MOBO Award-winner, Bashy), Lorraine Toussaint (Orange is the New Black), and Wilf Scolding (Cabaret).
The global phenomenon gallops home to the National Theatre.
New Born is a play bridging interconnected monologues that bring three lost souls together.
*What Happened Was* is a tender drama about two co-workers who meet for a first date.

shows.t: Henry VI: A Trilogy in Two Parts
shows.syn: Shakespeare’s history trilogy traces political collapse from foreign wars to civil conflict. Spanning decades of political upheaval, this adaptation of Shakespeare’s Henry VI trilogy charts England’s descent into instability following the death of Henry V. With an infant king on the throne, competing factions wage battles abroad while internal divisions deepen. The narrative continues nearly 30 years later as rivalries escalate into the War of the Roses, marking a prolonged period of civil war and shifting power. The production is adapted and directed by Stephen Brown-Fried, whose work includes staging classical texts in contemporary contexts. The text is drawn from the plays of William Shakespeare, one of the most widely produced playwrights in the theatrical canon. Presented by NAATCO...
'Are you sure That we are awake? It seems to me That yet we sleep, we dream.’

Zafar flees homophobic persecution in Pakistan to seek asylum in the UK. Londoner Bilal (self-styled as ‘Billy’) is ground down by years of Grindr and the complexity of being a brown gay man. Their worlds are about to change forever.
Two women. A chance encounter that tumbles into infatuation. And an undeniable force waiting just out of sight, ready to wreck it all.

World premiere of London’s thrilling new musical. Astronaut Daniel vanishes into space, leaving Emily behind, as their passionate, turbulent love story unfolds through flashbacks and spacelogs. Originally developed by the National Theatre, written by Theo Jamieson, directed by Adam Lenson, and starring Poppy Gilbert, Stuart Thompson, Gina Beck, Rupert Young, and Simbi Akande.

shows.t: School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play
shows.syn: "School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play" is a play set in 1986 Ghana that explores the dynamics and power struggles among a group of teenage girls at an elite secondary school as they compete for the chance to represent their school in the Miss Ghana pageant. The play delves into themes of colorism, privilege, and the social hierarchies that exist within the school's walls.

A time-shifting portrait of a woman and a Midwestern town in crisis. Set in a small Midwestern town, Well, I’ll Let You Go explores the intersecting struggles of a woman, her community, and her marriage in the aftermath of a crumbling American Dream. Moving between past and present, the play traces the unraveling of personal and collective histories, portraying both the vast scope of a town in decline and the intimate details of one life within it.
*The Unbelievers* is a new play about the power of faith and one family's search for answers.

shows.t: Horrible Histories: Barmy Britain - The Best Bits
shows.syn: We all want to meet people from history. The trouble is everyone is dead! So get ready for Horrible Histories live on stage with the best of Barmy Britain!

The finest acrobatic and cabaret talent from around the world are serving an intoxicating blend of vintage French glamour, high-end spectacle and titillating acts to infatuate, illuminate and inspire.
New York, 1930. A world of moonshine, racketeers, and jazz.

In the small hours of the morning on a New England college campus, middle-aged history professor George and his brash wife Martha return home from a faculty party and welcome unsuspecting younger guests, biology instructor Nick and his timid wife Honey, for a nightcap. As the liquor flows, George and Martha draw the couple into vicious rounds of marital warfare, humiliation, and psychological games, culminating in the shattering of a long-held illusion that has sustained their union.

London, 1890, a city rapidly expanding, devouring all in its path. Fresh off the success of his first big case, Sherlock Holmes misuses his time, until an unknown woman and a mysterious jewel arrive at 221b Baker Street. As the chase begins, and with lives on the line, can Holmes and Watson pull back the curtain on the big show and reveal the mastermind behind this deadly conspiracy.

ct.n: William Gillette, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle

shows.syn: This digital concert is unlike anything you’ve ever experienced before. Live musicians accompany digital avatars of the hit band ABBA in a totally new form of hybrid entertainment. Designed by the group themselves, you’ve never seen ABBA– or any concert– quite like this. Get your tickets to *ABBA Voyage* at their purpose-built venue the ABBA Arena today.
Step into the intoxicating world of Buenos Aires nightlife, where passion, drama and desire are brought vividly to life through the most sensual of dances: the Argentine tango.

Matthew Bourne’s award-winning The Car Man is back! Loosely based on Bizet’s ever-popular opera, The Car Man has one of the most thrilling and instantly recognisable scores in New Adventures’ repertoire.

After touring in Europe with audiences of over 300,000 people and a sold-out first run at the Peacock Theatre in 2024, the critically- acclaimed Stories is coming back to London for 20 new performances.

At Christmas, Nora Helmer returns from shopping carrying many packages and presents. Her husband, Torvald, is working in his study. He playfully rebukes Nora for spending so much money on Christmas gifts, calling her his "little squirrel". He teases her about how, the previous year, she had spent weeks making gifts and ornaments by hand because money was scarce.

In the first scene, a timid Graham approaches Tinker, who appears to be a drug dealer. He says he 'wants out' and also asks for drugs. Tinker refuses. They then have an argument about whether or not they are friends. Tinker eventually injects Graham with drugs and he overdoses and dies. Rod and Carl sit in a room together, Carl asks Rod if he can have his ring as a proposal of marriage.

Desire Under the Elms is a 1924 play written by Eugene O'Neill. Like Mourning Becomes Electra, Desire Under the Elms signifies an attempt by O'Neill to adapt plot elements and themes of Greek tragedy to a rural New England setting. It was inspired by the myth of Phaedra, Hippolytus, and Theseus. A film version was produced in 1958, and there is an operatic setting by Edward Thomas.
