Andrew Doherty: Sad Gay AIDS Play
Katie Norris: Go West, Old Maid
Kiell Smith-Bynoe & Friends: Kool Story Bro
Jordan Gray: Is That A C*ck In Your Pocket, Or Are You Just Here To Kill Me?
Legend – The Music of Bob Marley
Robin Hood and the Merry Mandem
The Uncontainable Nausea of Alec Baldwin
GOD IS A WOMAN THE MUSICAL

shows.syn: A carnival themed immersive magic experience with the UK’s best close up magicians performing at your table inches from your eyes. The Magicians Table reimagines what the art of magic can be.
The GODZ return after a triumphant sell out season in July 2025, bearing even more acts, but just as little clothing.
Audiences will be transported into the jungle as the Olivier is transformed for this timeless classic tale of family, courage and loyalty. Directed by Indhu Rubasingham.

In April 1975 at "Dreamland", a Saigon bar and brothel, shortly before the end of the Vietnam War, it is Kim's first day as a bargirl. The seventeen-year-old peasant girl is hauled in by the Engineer, a French-Vietnamese hustler who owns the joint. Backstage, the girls ready themselves for the night's show, jeering at Kim's inexperience ("Overture / Backstage Dreamland").

shows.t: Hot Singles In Your Area Play D&D
NT Connections Double Bill: Cloud Busting & Ride or Die
Daisy Doris May: Big Night Out
MÁS SABE EL SAULO POR VIEJO...
shows.syn: Renowned comedian and improviser Saulo García returns to Repertorio with "Más sabe el Saulo por viejo", his eleventh production. This fun and reflective comedy explores life and the passage of time, featuring original songs, beloved characters, and improvisation that promises laughter and emotion in every performance.

shows.t: Jason Manford: A Manford All Seasons

shows.syn: Trainspotting is an upcoming stage musical written by Irvine Welsh with music and lyrics by Stephen McGuinness and Welsh, based on Welsh's novel of the same name and its film adaptation.

shows.t: Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody
shows.syn: *Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody* satirizes the hit TV show about hockey players falling in love.
From the Producers of The Illusionists, and inspired by Lionsgate’s worldwide blockbuster film franchise, comes the London premiere of Now You See Me Live.

Meet the nature-loving Cinderella, who lives on the edge of an enchanted forest where she once gardened and sang with her mother. After loss and silence settle over her home, she’s left with a sharp-tongued stepmother, two noisy stepsisters, and a house full of chores and shadows. But when a letter arrives, inviting all to a Garden Ball, Cinderella’s journey to find her true self begins – guided by the spirit of her mother and the magic of the forest.

shows.t: THIS IS NOT ABOUT ME. (59E59 Theaters)
Lauder: Scotland's Kilted King of Broadway

shows.syn: In 1960s Israel, a group of American tourists encounters the realities of life in the young nation. Phil, a middle-aged American separated from his wife, falls in love with Ruth, a recent widow visiting from the States, but their romance is complicated by Phil's inability to obtain a divorce under Israeli law. Around them, fellow tourist Clara Weiss searches comically for a husband among the kibbutzim.

The play opens on a May day in the nursery of Lyubov Andreyevna Ranevskaya's home in the provinces of Russia, at the start of the 20th century. Ranevskaya has been living in France since her young son drowned. After she tried to kill herself, Ranevskaya's 17-year-old daughter Anya and Anya's governess Charlotta Ivanovna have brought her home, accompanied by Yasha, Ranevskaya's valet.
A contemporary family wakes up in a Greek myth and can’t seem to find a way out of their hellish destiny.

After a billion years of bad dates, Earth has finally found the one... Humanity. Sparks fly. Seeds are sown. Ground is broken. But what begins as a passionate love affair between the universe’s most iconic couple quickly descends into a hot mess. An original pop musical about love, hope, and the ultimate break

Inter Alia is the new play from Suzie Miller, the writer of Prima Facie. Jessica Parks is a sharp, funny Crown Court judge at the top of her game, balancing the demands of the bench with life as a wife and mother, until a crisis close to home tests everything she believes about justice.
An astonishing reinvention of circus, 360 ALLSTARS will leave you dizzy with excitement!
This New York Times Critic’s Pick is bringing joy to Broadway through January 5 only.

Desperate to escape their unhappy fates, young lovers Demetrius, Lysander, Helena and Hermia flee Athens for the moonlit woods. There – along with a band of amateur actors – they fall under the spell of mischievous fairy Puck and tumble into a dream world where illusion and reality are hilariously confused.

A fly-by-night office in Chicago. A brutal sales competition: Top dog wins a Cadillac. Second wins a set of steak knives. Third and fourth get fired. Four real estate agents cheat, fight and steal to come out on top — but can any of them win?

shows.v: The Laura Pels Theatre at the Harold and Miriam Steinberg Center for Theatre
shows.syn: Based on the hit film, *A Walk on the Moon* is the stirring new musical about one mother's great leap into her own future.

After suffering a stroke at 30 caused by a literal hole in her heart, comedian Cat Cohen transforms this near-death experience into a wildly funny, song-filled one-woman show about mortality, hypochondria and the undeniable thrill of being the main character. Equal parts confessional comedy and sparkling musical cabaret, Broad Strokes is Cohen at her sharpest, funniest, and most fabulously vulnerable.

Step inside a tale that seduced 1890s Paris - the world’s first cabaret club as The Lost Estate recreates the legendary cabaret Le Chat Noir. Includes a three-course banquet of decadent Parisian haute cuisine. A wild, intoxicating blend of world-class performance, immersive theatre, and haute cuisine — a spectacular only-in-London experience.

White Rabbit Red Rabbit, Iranian playwright Nassim Soleimanpour’s internationally acclaimed theatrical experiment, returns to London for its 15th anniversary. A rotating cast - including David Tennant, Riz Ahmed and Kathryn Hunter - steps on stage each night to open a sealed envelope and perform a script they’ve never seen before. No rehearsal. No director. No two performances are the same.

Emmy, two-time Tony, Screen Actors Guild and Drama Desk winner Christine Baranski makes her West End debut as the iconic Judith Bliss, sparring with Academy Award nominated stage and screen legend Richard E. Grant in a stinging new production of Noël Coward’s irresistible comedy directed by Emily Burns.

A mysterious virus devastates civilisation, leaving one man alone in bunker B-103. With enough supplies to survive, he isolates himself from the outside world - but as time passes, his reality begins to fracture. This one-person musical blends psychological thriller, gig and video diary with a live rock score.
More than thirty years after the Oscar and Golden Globe-winning film, writer Callie Khouri reimagines her iconic road movie, Thelma & Louise, as a brand-new musical.

A courtroom drama on Lenny Bruce’s 1964 obscenity trial and free speech rights. Set in 1964 New York City, the play dramatizes the obscenity trial of comedian Lenny Bruce, whose work and language led to legal prosecution. Drawing from the real case handled by attorney Marty Garbus, the narrative examines the legal arguments, testimonies, and cultural tensions surrounding freedom of speech during a pivotal moment in American history. The production is written by Susan Charlotte and directed by Antony Marsellis. It is based on Garbus’s firsthand experience defending Bruce, forming part of a trilogy of plays centered on civil liberties cases.
*Label•less* is a new musical experience that gives voice to today's issues, sharing the resilience needed to overcome barriers.

Nigeria, 2014. Teenagers Tisana, Haleema, and Ruha are best friends, busy swapping notes on celebrities, sex positions, and dodging carbs. But when they’re kidnapped by militant insurgents and forced towards an uncertain future, they have only each other to turn to. As fear and religious differences begin to fracture their bond, how far can their friendship be tested before it breaks?
Starring Kathryn Hunter and Ben Whishaw, Eurotrash, directed by Walter Meierjohann, brings Christian Kracht’s international best-seller, in a new adaptation by Colin Teevan, to the stage.

This is Rambert; now, as they’ve always been; living and breathing dance DNA; committed to putting the spotlight on voices, visions and ideas shaping our world today. Dance that’s alive with urgency, energy and relevance.

Since the play's original run, Shaffer extensively revised his play, including changes to plot details; the following is common to all revisions. The composer Salieri is an old man, having long outlived his fame. Speaking directly to the audience, he claims to have used poison to assassinate Mozart and promises to explain himself.

A new musical about Sir Alexander Fleming and the discovery of penicillin, with a contemporary cautionary frame about antibiotic resistance. Music and lyrics by Robin Hiley, book by Becky Hope-Palmer, directed by Alex Howarth.
Arthur Miller's 1968 family drama about two estranged brothers reunited to dispose of their late father's belongings, confronting old wounds, regrets and the choices that shaped their lives.

shows.t: And Then The Rodeo Burned Down
shows.syn: The rodeo is the best place in the world. Why would anybody burn it down? Dale, a rodeo clown with a big dream (and a mischievous shadow), certainly wouldn’t. After all, Dale wants to be a cowboy. So, if we’re going to find out who burned the rodeo down, we’ll have to finish the play. And now there’s fire involved? That sounds expensive.

shows.t: What We Talk About When We Talk About Anne Frank

shows.syn: Jamie Lloyd's blockbuster West End revival of the Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice musical, starring Rachel Zegler as Eva Perón. The production became a viral phenomenon for staging 'Don't Cry For Me Argentina' from the Palladium balcony to crowds gathered on Argyll Street.

shows.t: Morgan Bassichis: Can I Be Frank?
shows.syn: *Can I Be Frank?* is a new solo show from comedian Morgan Bassichis that pays homage to another queer comedian, Frank Maya, who died of from AIDS-related complications.
Get ready to see the world more curiously, because Blippi is coming London in the all-new Be Like Blippi Tour!

shows.t: My Son’s A Queer (But What Can You Do?)
shows.syn: My Son’s a Queer (But What Can You Do?) is the joyous autobiographical story of West End Musical Theatre star and social-media sensation Rob Madge, as they set out to recreate that parade - and this time, nobody, no, nobody is gonna rain on it.

shows.t: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button

shows.syn: An acclaimed solo show, *Small* is about big dreams — both on the race track and on Broadway.

shows.t: There's a Bear on My Chair
shows.syn: They’re a mischievous pair, are the mouse and the bear… pull up a seat for puppets aplenty and lots of laughs as Ross Collins’ books come alive on stage.

shows.t: James Baldwin A Life And Legacy With Ben Okri
Raising Hare An Evening With Chloe Dalton
Nt Live All My Sons 12a Tbc
Why I Stuck A Flare Up My Arse For England (Soho Playhouse)
shows.syn: A solo play tracing a football fan’s viral stunt and search for identity. The play follows Billy Kinley, an avid football supporter whose impulsive act during Euro 2020 sends him viral and alters the course of his life. What begins as a moment of spectacle unfolds into a personal account of loyalty, masculinity, and belonging, as Billy reflects on the culture that shaped him and the consequences of being suddenly seen. Structured as a solo performance, the work blends humor with candid self-examination, using the incident as a lens to explore identity and fandom. Why I Stuck a Flare Up My Arse for England has received multiple awards, including recognition at the Adelaide Fringe, and has toured internationally with a series of critically acclaimed runs.

1984. East Germany. A writer and an actor are placed under state surveillance. From the attic above their apartment, their Stasi man listens for evidence of subversion. But to observe a life is to risk changing your own.

A family comedy about grief, faith, and an unexpected celebration of Sukkot. One year after the death of his wife, Patrick Sullivan remains consumed by grief until a rabbi introduces him to the Jewish holiday of Sukkot, a festival centered on joy and gathering. Inspired by the idea of celebration as an obligation rather than a feeling, Patrick builds a sukkah in the family yard and insists that his three adult children join him as they return home for their mother’s unveiling ceremony. The play follows a half-Jewish, half-Irish-Catholic family attempting to navigate unfamiliar traditions while confronting loss, resentment, and connection. Through humor and family conflict, the story examines mourning, cultural identity, and the uneasy process of rebuilding community after absence.

shows.t: Hershey Felder: The Piano and Me
shows.syn: A pianist recounts his life and heritage through music and storytelling. In this solo play, Hershey Felder portrays himself alongside multiple figures from his past, tracing his upbringing in Montreal as the child of Polish and Hungarian immigrants. The narrative follows his early discovery of the piano and how music became a connection to his cultural roots while shaping his personal and professional path. As his story unfolds, key moments of opportunity, loss, and artistic development are explored through performance and reflection. The production incorporates live renditions of works by composers including Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin, Liszt, Rachmaninoff, and Bartók, using these pieces to frame the experiences that informed Felder’s career and extensive performance history.

Get ready to witness the incredible untold life story and music of multi-platinum selling, 10-time GRAMMY® winner and global icon, Chaka Khan! With 22 albums, 25 chart-topping hits, 70 million records sold and a career spanning five decades, Chaka Khan has shaped the sound of generations. Now, her story explodes onto stage starring Alexandra Burke (Sister Act, The Bodyguard, Chicago, The X Factor winner 2008) for a limited season at London’s Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre.

In addition to solo excerpts, the show combines passages from various autobiographies to create unforgettable ensemble "mash-ups" that ping-pong into riotously funny "he said, she said" scenarios, famous love triangles, and wildly different takes on the same experience.

Mr and Mrs X.E, are a desperate couple facing financial crisis and a crumbling marriage and they long for a better life. They discover two bruised and battered angels in their garden, they bring them inside to nurse them back to life. Care quickly turns to control. The couple seize the opportunity to exploit the spiritual beings in pursuit of fame and fortune.

Following the critical success of Dead Man Walking in 2025, ENO’s Artistic Director Annilese Miskimmon reimagines this timeless opera, exploring the art of resistance and love in the face of political censorship.

In a world shaped by war, Kaija Saariaho’s opera, Adriana Mater finds hope where it seems impossible. Powerful and rarely staged, this ENO debut unites Artistic Director Annilese Miskimmon and Music Director Designate André de Ridder in their first collaboration.

shows.t: Iphigenie en Tauride - English National Opera
shows.syn: A family divided by destiny, reunited by hope. Gluck’s rarely performed opera, Iphigénie en Tauride makes its ENO debut in a new staging for 2026/27 by Olivier award-winning director Lyndsey Turner.

shows.t: Breaking the Waves - English National Opera
shows.syn: This hauntingly beautiful opera explores faith, heartbreak and loss with unflinching emotional intensity. Emerging as one of the most powerful contemporary operas of our time and adapted from Lars von Trier’s critically acclaimed film, Missy Mazzoli’s Breaking the Waves comes to ENO in a striking new production for 2026/27.

shows.t: Trial By Jury & The Zoo - English National Opera
shows.syn: Trial by Jury & The Zoo come together in this wildly entertaining pairing. Acting as the prequel and sequel to the same ill‑fated love story, these rarely performed works are full of wit, absurdity and unexpected twists.

shows.t: Yamato, The Drummers of Japan: Hito no Chikara - The Power of Human Strength
shows.syn: After electrifying London audiences in 2019 and again in 2024 with Wings of the Phoenix, YAMATO now unveil their brand-new production: Hito no Chikara – The Power of Human Strength.
Sharp tongues and savage gossip fuel a messy, magnetic attraction in this new production of Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing in the Globe Theatre.

Three workers navigate a controversial NYC landmark turned viral spectacle. Set at the site of a widely publicized New York City landmark, the play follows three minimum wage parks employees working at a towering interactive structure in Hudson Yards. As the installation becomes a subject of viral attention and repeated shutdowns, the trio must contend with its growing notoriety while managing their day-to-day responsibilities. Their interactions unfold against the backdrop of a space that shapes both their work environment and public scrutiny. The play is written by Brendan George and directed by Peter Charney. It is produced by Through The Tollbooth Co., a company focused on developing new theatrical works. The creative team previously collaborated on A Eulogy for Roman, which receive...

shows.t: The House of the Negro Insane
shows.syn: A historical drama set inside a segregated psychiatric hospital in 1935 America. Set in 1935, the play follows Attius, a long-term resident of Central State Hospital, one of several psychiatric institutions in the United States designated for Black patients labeled “insane and idiotic.” Within the hospital walls, the homeless, impoverished, ill, and criminally institutionalized are housed together under harsh conditions. Attius survives by building coffins for patients who die inside the institution, carrying out his work in isolation and resignation. The arrival of two new patients disrupts the fragile routine he has constructed for himself. As relationships form and old hopes resurface, Attius begins to confront the possibility of a life beyond confinement. The play examines instituti...
Director Dominic Cooke reunites with multi award-winning playwright Caryl Churchill to direct the play which examines the complexities of identity and change.

shows.t: The Rise and Fall of Little Voice
shows.syn: Robert Hastie directs this new production of Jim Cartwright's modern classic.

Three hikers share a woodland shelter in Stephen Sheffer’s comedy-drama. An overprepared hiker and a less-prepared couple unexpectedly find themselves sharing a rustic lean-to shelter deep in the woods. As the strangers swap supplies, stories, and conversations about escaping city life, their brief retreat becomes a space for unexpected intimacy and emotional honesty. Around the campfire, moments of humor and connection gradually reveal tensions beneath the surface. The play is written by Stephen Sheffer and directed by Jesse Jou. The production is presented by New Light Theater Project in association with Pendragon Theatre at 59E59 Theaters. The creative team includes scenic designer Connor Gallerani, costume designer Krista Grevas, lighting designer Elaine Wong, sound designer Jennie ...

shows.t: Crazy Mama: A True Story of Love and Madness
shows.syn: A daughter fights to hold her family together through her mother’s mental illness. Based on Sharon Scott Williams’ memoir, this play follows a young girl growing up in a family shaped by her mother’s recurring institutionalization and struggles with mental illness. As her mother becomes convinced she is working for the FBI and is repeatedly committed to psychiatric facilities, the family attempts to cope in different ways: her father turns to alcohol, while her brother wrestles with questions of faith. At the center of the story is Sharon’s determination to remain connected to her mother despite years of instability and separation. Combining live music with autobiographical storytelling, the play traces the long emotional impact of caregiving, hope, and survival within a fractured family.
*Paranormal Activity* is a play based on the cult film about a haunting that follows a young couple.

This is a love story. It’s hands that smell of Dolce and Gabbana Light Blue after days spent clutching fistfulls of her hair. It’s the rain hitting the earth in a way that reminds you of blood, that makes you think the world's holding a knife to your underwear. It’s the spins. It’s running out of air because you gulped too much of it while you were sobbing. It’s waking up hot and sticky. It’s desperately falling in love with your best friend inside a camping tent while everything outside rages.
*Shifters* is the intimate story of two old friends whose lives pull them apart, only for them to boomerang back to each other.

shows.t: The Mystery of Edwin Drood (AMT Theater)
shows.syn: A theatrical murder mystery where the audience decides who killed Edwin Drood. This musical mystery is structured as a Victorian-era performance troupe staging Charles Dickens’ unfinished novel The Mystery of Edwin Drood. When Edwin Drood disappears under suspicious circumstances, the company presents a growing list of possible suspects whose rivalries, hidden motives, and personal entanglements complicate the investigation. As the story unfolds, revelations and reversals continually reshape the mystery. Because Dickens never completed the original novel, the production incorporates audience participation, allowing each performance to determine the identity of the murderer and the final outcome of the narrative.

shows.t: Are You Now or Have You Ever Been?
shows.syn: This summer, in a strictly limited engagement, a rotating all-star cast comes together for a timely and important revival of Eric Bentley's ARE YOU KNOW OR HAVE YOU EVER BEEN. This electrifying docudrama drops you into the tense world of the 1940s House Committee on Un-American Activities hearings, where fame offered no protection and political pressure could end a career.

shows.t: Jesus Christ Superstar - Theatre Royal Drury Lane
shows.syn: The award-winning Regent's Park Open Air Theatre production of __Jesus Christ Superstar__ is extending to __Theatre Royal Drury Lane__ due to record-breaking demand for the summer season at __The London Palladium__. Starring __Sam Ryder__ as Jesus in his West End debut.
Welcome to the club. Red lights. Oiled abs. Dollar bills. Three men about to make you feel things you weren’t expecting. Grab front row seats to get up close and very personal.

shows.t: Catarina and the Beauty of Killing Fascists

shows.syn: Cate Blanchett and Nina Hoss reunite on stage

Julie Robson is used to being overlooked. But when an encounter on a station platform goes wrong and all eyes are suddenly on Julie, something shifts and she feels compelled to make a stand. Anne-Marie Duff is Julie in this provocative new play from Helen Edmundson, directed by Blanche McIntyre.

A musical exploring inherited trauma, activism, and the legacy of the Greensboro Massacre. The musical draws on the 1979 Greensboro Massacre, in which five labor organizers were killed during a protest in Greensboro, North Carolina. It follows a narrative shaped by the aftermath of that violence, tracing how its impact extends across generations. What begins as an attempt to document history evolves into a broader exploration of memory, trauma, and the lingering presence of unresolved events. Created by César James Alvarez, who was born into the survivor community, the musical shifts between personal reflection and collective experience. Featuring a 12-person intergenerational cast, the work incorporates music and storytelling to examine capitalism, solidarity, and how individuals proce...

Step into a prehistoric world of astonishing (and remarkably life-like) creatures. Meet an incredible line-up of dinosaurs, including every child’s favourite flesh-eating giant, the Tyrannosaurus Rex, alongside a Triceratops, Giraffatitan, Microraptor and Segnosaurus.

In this Italian opera, a mysterious Chinese princess named Turandot refuses to marry and instead challenges all suitors to solve three riddles—those who fail are executed. When an unknown prince arrives and successfully answers her riddles, Turandot attempts to escape her pledge by posing him a final test: she must discover his name by dawn, or she will marry him. The prince, aided by his faithful slave girl Liu who loves him, gambles that Turandot will fall in love with him before sunrise.
Puccini’s melodrama about a volatile diva, a sadistic police chief, and an idealistic artist has thrilled audiences for more than a century.
Donizetti's "Maria Stuarda" explores the political and personal rivalry between Mary, Queen of Scots, and Queen Elizabeth I of England.
Gustavo Dudamel makes his Met debut leading Verdi’s towering Shakespearean masterpiece, in the first revival of Bartlett Sher’s production.
A vivid, seductive staging, featuring a monumental setting for the last-act Temple of Dagon, where the hero crushes his Philistine enemies.

shows.v: The Arts at Marble Arch powered by TodayTix
shows.syn: Welcome to Westerberg High, where popularity is a matter of life and death and Veronica Sawyer is just another of the nobodies dreaming of a better day.

First seen 45 years ago, the Olivier Award-winning and much-loved Jeeves Takes Charge returns to London for a short season at the Charing Cross Theatre after showcase productions at the Jermyn Street Theatre, The Tabard Theatre, and a Christmas season at the Theatre Royal, Bath.

A high-tech magic show blending classic illusions with interactive, immersive audience experiences. Following its run in London’s West End and a record-setting engagement in Chicago, this production features magician Jamie Allan, known for integrating digital technology with traditional sleight of hand. The show incorporates interactive elements that invite audience participation, using tools such as smartphones, lasers, and holograms. Allan’s approach merges classic illusions with contemporary tech, creating a hybrid format that emphasizes both spectacle and interactivity. Now presented in New York City, the performance continues Allan’s exploration of how magic can evolve through the use of modern media and immersive techniques.

August Wilson’s landmark play, set in the 1950s, returns in a vital new production directed by the award-winning Daniel Bailey (Red Pitch, West End). From one of America’s most influential 20th century writers, this is a story of ambition for our time.

Guests attend a 1914 séance where secrets and beliefs are put to the test. Set in 1914, this immersive play takes place during a private séance hosted by the eccentric Madame Montfort. The gathering is disrupted by the arrival of a mysterious guest, prompting those in attendance to confront their beliefs about love, the supernatural, and the unknown. Among the participants are a skeptical magician, a paranormal researcher, and a practitioner of blood rituals, each bringing conflicting perspectives to the unfolding events. Presented in spit&vigor’s “embedded” immersive style, the production places audience members within the séance itself, seated among the performers as observers to the escalating tensions and revelations.

With a new arrival on the way the whole family are busy getting ready. With building and decorating work to be done it’s an oinktastic makeover and Peppa Pig, Mummy Pig, Daddy Pig & George all need your help to get everything ready before the big day. There’s so much to do – will they get it all finished in time?

Based on the beloved Disney Channel film, join Troy, Gabriella and the students of East High as they navigate the highs and lows of first love, friendship and self-discovery — all while juggling classes, basketball games, auditions and the expectations of their peers.

Allegra is full of joy. So much of it that she cannot stop herself from bursting into song. At home, in the street, even in shops and restaurants. Sometimes the music is only a fantasy in her head. But at other times, it results in a loud and disruptive performance that causes chaos in the village where she lives. Allegra’s brother, Ronen, and her carer, Anna, must somehow control her eccentricities and avoid angry visits by the local policeman. But is this possible without destroying the great

Inspired by La Bohème, Rent follows a group of young artists and dreamers in New York's East Village as they navigate poverty, love, loss and the AIDS crisis — living fiercely and fully in the moment. Raw, joyful and heartbreaking in equal measure, it remains one of the most vital musicals ever written.

Essex, 1977. Beverly is hosting, the alcohol is flowing, Demis Roussos is on the record player and the cheese and pineapple cocktail sticks are ready to go. Queen of the castle in her suburban semi, Beverly and husband Laurence welcome new neighbours Angela and Tony round for drinks.
After a record shattering sold out run, it’s back for round two. Ready to ride again?

Following its acclaimed Off-Broadway run, The Jonathan Larson Project makes its European premiere in London. Directed by John Simpkins, the production celebrates the visionary creator of Rent and tick, tick... BOOM! through previously unheard songs, while marking 30 years since Jonathan Larson’s untimely death.

A period drama about poets and critics confronting art’s changing cultural power. Set in Frenchtown, New Jersey in the summer of 1939, the play follows poet Delmore Schwartz, writer Gertrude Buckman, and poet and critic James Agee during a shared weekend on the eve of World War II. Against the backdrop of a rapidly changing cultural landscape, their conversations and relationships reveal tensions between literature, poetry, and the growing influence of film in American life. Inspired by real historical figures, the play examines a transitional moment in artistic culture, tracing how cinema began to eclipse poetry and literature as a dominant force in shaping public imagination and understanding. The story draws on the lives of Delmore Schwartz, Gertrude Buckman, and James Agee.

Two teens at a Christian summer camp confront faith, desire, and identity. Forced to share a room at a conservative Christian summer camp, Ryan and Jabez begin the week expecting conflict rather than connection. Ryan appears composed and devout, while Jabez resists the camp’s rigid expectations with open cynicism. As late-night conversations deepen into attraction, the two are drawn into an increasingly risky emotional bond that challenges their understanding of faith, identity, and belonging. Set within the controlled environment of a religious camp, the play explores the tension between personal desire and institutional expectation. As pressures from the outside world intrude, Ryan and Jabez must decide whether protecting themselves means abandoning the connection they have found with...

BROKEN SNOW is a tense psychological thriller set in an abandoned house where strangers are drawn into a dangerous game of suspicion, memory, and buried truths.  What begins as a chance encounter becomes a gripping confrontation charged with secrets, shifting power, and the threat of violence. With each revelation, the line between hunter and hunted grows harder to define in this riveting new play about survival, identity, and the devastating cost of uncovering what was meant to stay hidden.

A governess risks scandal after rebelling against the life imposed on her. Written by Cicely Hamilton in 1911, PHYL follows Phyllis Chester, a governess trapped in an isolated and restrictive existence. Frustrated by the limitations placed on her life and desires, she acts impulsively in a way that threatens her social standing and future. The play examines questions of female independence, sexuality, and respectability within the constraints of early 20th-century society. Originally banned from performance at Oxford University despite passing official censorship without required edits, the play instead premiered in Manchester, where contemporary critics reacted strongly to its treatment of women’s desire and personal freedom. Hamilton described the work as a comedy with a happy ending,...

Visitors are welcome to take a guided tour of the Park Avenue Armory with one of our staff and view the unique qualities of this landmark building, from the soaring 55,000 square foot Wade Thompson Drill Hall to the extraordinary interiors by Louis Comfort Tiffany, Stanford White, Candace Wheeler, Herter Brothers and others.
*The Black Mirror Experience* blends physical and actual realty to create a unique, immersive show based on the hit TV series and set at a tech giant.

A Tony Award-winning family drama revival about memory, loyalty, and a memoir that threatens to expose the past. Other Desert Cities is set on Christmas Eve in a Palm Springs home, where the Wyeth family—politically connected and outwardly composed—is upended when a daughter returns with a memoir threatening to bring long-buried secrets into the open. What follows is a confrontation between memory, loyalty, and legacy, as old wounds resurface and the family is forced to reckon with competing claims over their shared history and who has the right to tell it. Written by Jon Robin Baitz, the play originally won the Tony Award for Best Play revival and returns to Broadway in a new production directed by John Benjamin Hickey. The cast is led by Julia Louis-Dreyfus (Veep, Seinfeld), Ed Harris...
*Evita* is the riveting story of the rise and fall of the glamorous First Lady of Argentina.

Mermaids & Pirates features a shipload of unforgettable characters, including the Seasick Pirate, a crazy castaway and Isla, Queen of the Island. Packed with calypso-infused songs, salsa-styled choreography and plenty of comic surprises, this one-hour musical celebrates teamwork, courage and the magic of the Caribbean.

shows.t: All The Things We Cant Explain

shows.syn: Two exes. One dinner. What could go wrong?

Tom is travelling in Berlin with no hostel and no plan. When Charlotte, a native Berliner working in a bar, offers him the use of her couch, he can't believe his luck. Intoxicated by one another, they want to lose themselves to desire. But as night becomes morning, secrets emerge that cannot be ignored.

Four girls' sleepovers and The Sims blur adolescence, friendship, and agency. In suburban Central Ohio, four girls gather every week for a sleepover. They talk, gossip, snack, experiment with drinking, and spend hours playing The Sims, a life-simulation computer game. As they navigate friendship and adolescence, questions emerge about identity, visibility, and how much control they have over the lives they are trying to shape. The play examines the people who know you before you know yourself. The play is written by Eliya Smith and directed by Chloe Claudel. The production features choreography by Lena Engelstein, scenic design by Forest Entsminger, costume design by Olivia Vaughn Hern, lighting design by Abigail Sage and Finn Bamber, and sound design by Mitchell Polonsky.

17-time Grammy Award winning artist Sting will perform in this new production of his musical, The Last Ship; featuring a new book by Barney Norris and direction by Leo Warner with Set and Video Design by 59 Studio.
*The Fantasticks* is the beloved musical about neighbors who pretend to feud to get their children to fall in love.
*Gloria* is a play about a cut-throat magazine and how writers use the aftermath of an office event to further their own careers.

shows.v: The Irene Diamond Stage at the Pershing Square Signature Center
The Irene Diamond Stage at the Pershing Square Signature Center

shows.t: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater - New Works
shows.syn: A mixed bill of contemporary dance featuring three UK premieres alongside two established works. The programme spans intimate duets, spiritual meditations and athletic ensemble pieces — all anchored in powerful musical partnerships — and closes with Alvin Ailey s iconic Revelations, the most widely seen modern dance work in the world.

Giant is a 2024 play written by Mark Rosenblatt. It premiered at the Royal Court Theatre in 2024 in a production starring John Lithgow as Roald Dahl and won three Laurence Olivier Awards, including Best New Play.

Giant is a 2024 play written by Mark Rosenblatt. It premiered at the Royal Court Theatre in 2024 in a production starring John Lithgow as Roald Dahl and won three Laurence Olivier Awards, including Best New Play.

shows.t: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater - Legacy
shows.syn: A programme of Alvin Ailey classics spanning six decades, from the jazz-infused playfulness of Night Creature to the spiritual power of Grace and Cry — closing, as ever, with the iconic Revelations.

Two friends chase dreams, desire, and disaster in this quirky musical comedy. In the Dukes is a lively two-person musical comedy that blends sharp humor, catchy songs, and absurd misadventures. Created and performed by Saturday Night Live cast member Jane Wickline and comedian Liva Pierce, the show follows two friends navigating ambition, attraction, and the pursuit of their biggest dreams. Featuring a piano, plenty of misguided confidence, and at least one spectacular mistake, this playful production explores desire, friendship, and the fine line between brilliance and foolishness with wit and charm.

shows.v: The Romulus Linney Courtyard Theatre at The Pershing Square Signature Center
shows.syn: This sharp, timely thriller examines how a new tech opportunity impacts the lives of four friends.

George wishes he wasn't the scruffiest giant in town. But after a trip to a fancy clothes shop, he has a spectacular new look: smart trousers, a smart shirt, a stripy tie, and shiny shoes. Now he’s the smartest giant in town... until he bumps into some animals who desperately need his help - and his clothes!
The Public Theater’s Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Romeo and Juliet at the Delacorte Theater in Central Park, directed by Saheem Ali.

When Fiona Foster and Bob Phillips are each accused of having an affair by their spouses, they use the innocent and unsuspecting Featherstones as an alibi, dragging them into a web of chaos and confusion. As the lives of the three couples intertwine, the lies deepen and mayhem ensues in one of theatre’s most entertaining comedies.

Directed by multi award-winner Nicholas Hytner (The History Boys, One Man, Two Guvnors, Giant) and starring Olivier Award winner Rory Kinnear (Skyfall, The Diplomat) and Royal Ballet principal Natalia Osipova in her West End debut, this blazing new play tells the astonishing story of rebel economist and member of the Bloomsbury Group, John Maynard Keynes.
In this comedic thriller and West End hit, a woman believes her house is haunted, despite what her partner and friends think.

The  Science Theater Company, that presented more than 800 performances of THAT PHYSICS SHOW and THAT CHEMISTRY SHOW, returns to off-Broadway with THAT MATH SHOW.  In association with the National Museum Of Mathematics (MoMath), the show features Dr. Arthur Benjamin, a nationally known "math-e-magician".

Emma walks into Dexter’s life on the night of their graduation. One unsuspecting day that changes them both forever. But where will they be on this day next year? And the year after that? And every year that follows?
*860* is Billy Crystal's one-person show about the Los Angeles fires — and losing his own home.
A queer play about why and how we choose to pay attention. About the effort and sweat needed to build a life with someone. About whether love is enough to save us.

Lost in a world of surveillance and suspicion, one man fights to hold on to who he is and right this wrong. Based on true events, from debut writer Tafadzwa Muchenje and Stand and Be Counted’s Artistic Director Rosie MacPherson, Ripples is an urgent and electrifying interrogation of Britain’s treatment of migrants and the relentless power of hope.

Don’t miss the world premiere of *Insane Asylum Seekers*, the 2023 Tony Craze Award-winning play. This moving and hilarious story is a multi-generational tale spanning a century and exploring the British-Iraqi experience.

Tonight’s the night. She’s got a plan. And it involves her (secret) girlfriend, and the house they're about to move into together. And it doesn’t matter to her that her mum warns tonight is the first night of the ghost month. Because parents will say anything to keep you home.

Born under a blue sky in a city of lakes, a girl grows up with her father and sister. The three of them together, always. But as she grows, the land begins to change. A giant factory rises over her town. Her mother always wanted more for them - now the girl wants more too.

shows.syn: A brilliant girl uses courage and imagination to change her world in this musical. KOTA Productions brings the Tony Award-winning Matilda The Musical to the stage in a fresh and vibrant new production inspired by Roald Dahl’s beloved novel. Featuring a book by Dennis Kelly and an original score by Tim Minchin, the musical follows an extraordinary young girl whose intelligence, determination, and imagination help her overcome challenges and inspire those around her. Performed by a talented cast from across the country, this reimagined Off-Broadway staging celebrates the power of resilience, creativity, and standing up for what is right. Filled with memorable songs, humor, and heart, Matilda The Musical is an uplifting story about finding your voice and believing in the possibility of cha...

Rival paleontologists face judgment from dinosaurs in a musical comedy. Inspired by true events, this musical comedy follows 19th-century paleontologists O.C. Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope, whose intense rivalry fueled a race to uncover fossils across the United States. Their competition led to significant scientific discoveries, but their personal animosity and relentless pursuit of recognition ultimately damaged both their careers and reputations. The story reimagines their conflict in the afterlife, where a jury of dinosaurs is tasked with resolving the feud once and for all. As the two men revisit their achievements, mistakes, and grievances, the musical explores ambition, legacy, and the consequences of obsession through a comedic lens.

A new waitress sparks chaos in a dark comedy about service, desire, and collapse. Masticate is a darkly comic exploration of workplace tension, human desire, and the fragile balance that keeps everyday life functioning. Set inside a casual dining restaurant, the story follows the arrival of an enigmatic new waitress whose presence disrupts the establishment’s delicate social order. As stress mounts and hidden frustrations rise to the surface, the staff find themselves spiraling toward inevitable chaos. Blending sharp humor with biting social commentary, the play examines how people navigate anger, ambition, and personal connection while maintaining the illusion of excellent customer service. As the pressures of work and life intensify, Masticate reveals what happens when a seemingly ord...

A fallen movie star and her biggest fan team up to solve a murder and clear her name. Marlise is a mystery-filled drama that follows a once-famous Hollywood actress whose life is thrown into turmoil when she becomes the prime suspect in a murder case. With her reputation and future on the line, she reluctantly teams up with an intensely devoted fan whose fascination with her borders on obsession. As the unlikely pair investigates the crime, they uncover secrets, confront unexpected dangers, and navigate a complicated relationship built on admiration, distrust, and necessity. Blending suspense, intrigue, and dark humor, the story explores fame, identity, and the lengths people will go to in pursuit of the truth.

The Cornley crew battle miscommunication, delays to their set, actors missing in action and a growing feud over who will play the lead. It’s sure to be a disastrous take on the much-loved classic Christmas story of Ebenezer Scrooge. Will Cornley finally change their ways, or will their misfortunes wreak havoc yet again.

A new dance thriller, adapted from the film, following ballerina Nina as she is consumed by the pursuit of perfection in a high-stakes production of Swan Lake. World-premiere musical at American Repertory Theater with music and lyrics by Dave Malloy, directed and choreographed by Sonya Tayeh, and a book by Jen Silverman.
In this seven-time Olivier Award-winning musical for the whole family, a small, lost bear named Paddington travels from Peru to London, meets a family, and searches for home.

Bone Wars is a bold new musical comedy inspired by the unbelievable true story of Gilded Age paleontologists O.C. Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope. Their fierce rivalry led them to discover thousands of fossils, but their obsessive hatred destroyed them both. Now, more than a century after their deaths, a jury of dinosaurs will settle their historic feud — allowing one man to remain in the afterlife, and banishing the other to extinction.

World-premiere musical adaptation of R.J. Palacio's best-selling novel, with a book by Pulitzer finalist Sarah Ruhl and a score by A Great Big World (Ian Axel & Chad King), directed by Taibi Magar. Auggie Pullman, a boy with a facial difference, leaves homeschooling for the fraught world of middle school in search of acceptance.

shows.syn: A zealous man’s quest to save his town spirals into obsession and madness. Misterman is a powerful and unsettling portrait of faith, obsession, and psychological unraveling set in a small Irish town. Thomas Magill, a deeply devout evangelist, sees moral corruption everywhere around him—from neighbors he views as sinners to everyday behaviors he believes threaten the soul of the community. Convinced that he has been chosen to lead others toward salvation, Thomas embarks on a mission to reform the town, certain that God is guiding his actions. As his efforts are ignored and resisted, his grip on reality begins to weaken. Strange visions, intrusive thoughts, and mounting frustrations blur the line between spiritual conviction and dangerous fanaticism. Intensely theatrical and emotionally c...

shows.syn: On the day of his high school graduation party, Billy, a young man feeling at odds with his future before it has even begun, finds a trunk of letters written to him by his late mother, whom he’d been told abandoned him as a child. The discovery sets Billy and his best friend Scoot on a journey to uncover the truth about his past, and his connection to a woman he never knew, who might just be the key to understanding where he stands in the world.

Two hedgehogs confront survival, love, and an uncertain winter in dark woodland satire. Set in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, Day of the Hog follows two hedgehogs preparing for Groundhog Day as the prospect of six more weeks of winter threatens their home and survival. What begins as an absurdist woodland comedy gradually narrows its focus to the pressures of scarcity, partnership, and endurance as the shadow of Punxsutawney Phil hangs over their future. The play is a new work that blends animal fable, dark comedy, and social satire. Through the perspective of its hedgehog protagonists, the story examines how larger systems and traditions shape the lives of those with little power to influence them. shows.syn: A mentalism show from India's most-subscribed mentalist Suhani Shah blending mind-reading, comedy, and audience interaction. Spellbound is a solo mentalism show in which Suhani Shah weaves her own life story into an evening of increasingly extraordinary feats of mind-reading, comedy, and audience participation. Highly interactive in format, the show invites audience members to engage directly while remaining unpredictable for those who choose to observe. Shah moves between personal narrative and mentalism across the course of the evening, building toward an experience in which the audience becomes as much a part of the show as the performer herself. Shah began performing at age seven and has spent three decades building a career across more than 5,000 shows in 20 countries. She is the m...
Climb into a world of magic and mischief this festive season, as we welcome back “panto royalty” (The Times) Clive Rowe to the Hackney Empire stage for Jack and the Beanstalk.

A world-premiere bio-musical tracing the rise of TLC, the best-selling American girl group in history, through the lives of T-Boz, Left Eye, and Chilli. Written and directed by Kwame Kwei-Armah, set to two dozen songs from the TLC catalog including "Waterfalls," "No Scrubs," and "Creep." A Broadway-bound production at Arena Stage’s Kreeger Theater.

A world-premiere musical comedy — full title "Iceboy! Or, The Completely Untrue Story of How Eugene O'Neill Came to Write The Iceman Cometh" — starring Megan Mullally as a 1930s Broadway diva who adopts a 40,000-year-old Neanderthal, with Nick Offerman as Eugene O'Neill. Music by Mark Hollmann (Urinetown), directed by Marc Bruni (The Great Gatsby), closing the Goodman Theatre’s centennial season.

Berlin, 1933. With martial law in effect, political activism has become a capital crime.
A young Gestapo officer arrests a graduate student suspected of illegal research. This interrogation promises to be most challenging as he faces the iconic 20th-century thinker Hannah Arendt.
Is she innocent? Or an enemy of the state? Inspired by real events, this fantastical drama delves into the life and mind of one of history's most profound thinkers.

shows.syn: A woman finds her voice through songwriting in Lindsey Kraft's autobiographical solo musical. Liv is 40, codependent, and unexpectedly driven to write music. With no previous musical experience, she teaches herself piano while forming a relationship with a secret online confidant. As she writes a deeply personal collection of songs, she confronts family secrets, her father's addiction, years of silence, and the process of finding the confidence to stand on her own. Written, composed, and lyricized by Lindsey Kraft, the autobiographical one-woman musical draws on her own experience of discovering songwriting later in life. Kraft also stars in the production, joined onstage by acclaimed singer-songwriter Ben Folds and bassist Dan Rudin, who perform the live musical accompaniment. Presente...

With laughs and surprises for everyone, this is interactive theatre at its best.

shows.syn: A negotiator and an interpreter are called to a secret emergency meeting. Waiting for them are a chicken, a rat, a snow leopard and an army of voices from the natural world demanding an end to exploitation and ecological destruction.
Desperate to carve out an identity of his own to escape the shadow of his adored older brother, King John must step into the role he claims the right to and attempt to rule his England.
What begins as a play within a play soon becomes a gripping tale of art, ego and love. And, when the curtain falls, what is really left behind?

Are you a Faithful or a Traitor? Step inside the world of The Traitors and play the official live experience in Covent Garden. Complete missions, take your seat at The Round Table, build alliances and uncover hidden Traitors in a thrilling game of strategy, deception and trust. Will you survive as a Faithful or triumph as a Traitor? Just remember, even your closest ally could be your most dangerous enemy…

In the corridors of the Senate, a murderous plot builds amidst concerns over the growing ambition of dictator Julius Caesar. But when the tide of public opinion turns against his enemies, political in-fighting unfolds into civil war…

shows.syn: Presented in a relaxed picnic theatre style, the delightfully interactive pantomime Jack and the Beanstalk invites audiences of all ages to join in the adventure. Giggle at the Goose on the Loose, hunt for the Golden Eggs, sing along with Daisy the Cow, and help Jack defeat the Giant once and for all!

On the holiest day of the year, an idealistic young rabbi does the one thing nobody saw coming – he dares to challenge the billionaire president of his congregation, questions a multi-million-dollar donation, and ignites a battle for the hearts and minds of the entire community.

Shrek's Adventure! London is a walk-through immersive attraction on the South Bank in which visitors join Shrek, Donkey, and other DreamWorks characters on a mission through the fairytale world of Far Far Away. Guided across ten themed live-action sets and 4D experiences, guests must help thwart the witch Rumpelstiltskin, who has kidnapped Shrek and plans to unleash chaos on London.
*A View from the Bridge* is Arthur Miller's classic drama about a Brooklyn longshoreman and the dreams, deceit, and desire that surround relatives' visit.
